ko.title: [유통학 원론 #3] 왜 당신이 좋아하는 브랜드와 그 상품을 파는 매장은 조용히 싸우고 있을까

segments.src: > Every distribution channel runs on power, and wherever there's power there's conflict — the partnerships that win are the ones that turn a tug-of-war into a shared plan.
segments.tr: > 모든 유통 채널은 힘을 바탕으로 움직이며, 힘이 있는 곳에는 갈등이 따르기 마련입니다. 승리하는 파트너십은 힘겨루기를 공동의 계획으로 바꾸는 파트너십입니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: A product almost never travels straight from a factory to your hands.
segments.tr: 제품이 공장에서 소비자 손에까지 곧바로 도달하는 경우는 거의 없습니다.

segments.src: It passes through a **distribution channel**: manufacturer → distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: 제품은 **유통 채널(distribution channel)**—제조업체 → 유통업체 → 소매업체 → 소비자—을 거쳐 이동합니다.

segments.src: Each link is a separate company with its own P&L, its own boss, and its own definition of a good quarter.
segments.tr: 각 연결 고리는 저마다의 손익계산서(P&L), 각자의 상사, 그리고 좋은 분기에 대한 자신만의 정의를 가진 독립된 기업입니다.

segments.src: They need each other, but they don't want the same things.
segments.tr: 이들은 서로가 필요하지만, 원하는 것은 같지 않습니다.

segments.src: That gap is where **channel power** comes in.
segments.tr: 그 간극에서 바로 **채널 파워(channel power)**가 작용합니다.

segments.src: The simplest way to think about it:
segments.tr: 이를 이해하는 가장 간단한 방법은 다음과 같습니다:

segments.src: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you
segments.tr: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you

segments.src: ÷ how easily they could replace you
segments.tr: ÷ how easily they could replace you

segments.src: Retail textbooks usually break power into five sources (adapted from French and Raven's classic framework):
segments.tr: 유통 교과서에서는 대개 파워의 원천을 다섯 가지로 분류합니다(프렌치와 레이븐의 고전적인 프레임워크를 차용함):

segments.src: - **Reward power** — "Hit this volume and you get better terms, co-op ad dollars, early access to the new line."
segments.tr: - **보상적 파워(Reward power)** — "이 판매 물량을 달성하면 더 나은 조건, 공동 광고비 지원, 신제품 라인에 대한 우선 접근권을 드립니다."

segments.src: - **Coercive power** — "Miss the target and we cut your allocation, delay shipments, or give the endcap to someone else."
segments.tr: - **강압적 파워(Coercive power)** — "목표를 달성하지 못하면 할당량을 삭감하고, 배송을 지연하며, 엔드캡(매대 끝 진열대)을 다른 곳에 주겠습니다."

segments.src: - **Legitimate power** — "The contract says so." Rights spelled out in a franchise agreement or supply deal.
segments.tr: - **합법적 파워(Legitimate power)** — "계약서에 그렇게 명시되어 있습니다." 프랜차이즈 계약이나 공급 계약에 명시된 권리입니다.

segments.src: - **Expert power** — "We know this category better than you do." Category-management data, merchandising know-how, demand forecasts.
segments.tr: - **전문적 파워(Expert power)** — "우리가 이 카테고리를 당신보다 더 잘 압니다." 카테고리 관리 데이터, 머천다이징 노하우, 수요 예측 등이 여기에 해당합니다.

segments.src: - **Referent power** — "People want to be associated with us." A brand so desirable that retailers compete to carry it.
segments.tr: - **준거적 파워(Referent power)** — "사람들이 우리와 함께하고 싶어 합니다." 소매업체들이 서로 취급하려고 경쟁할 정도로 매력적인 브랜드입니다.

segments.src: Notice that power flows **both directions**.
segments.tr: 파워는 **양방향**으로 흐른다는 점에 주목하세요.

segments.src: A national brand has expert and referent power; a large chain has reward and coercive power because it controls shelf space and traffic.
segments.tr: 내국적 브랜드는 전문적 파워와 준거적 파워를 갖고 있으며, 대형 체인은 매장 공간과 트래픽을 통제하기 때문에 보상적 파워와 강압적 파워를 갖습니다.

segments.src: Neither side is automatically the boss.
segments.tr: 어느 한쪽이 일방적으로 '갑'이 되는 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: The party that effectively coordinates the channel is called the **channel captain** — sometimes the manufacturer, sometimes the retailer, sometimes a platform.
segments.tr: 채널을 효과적으로 조율하는 주체를 **채널 리더(channel captain)**라고 부릅니다. 때로는 제조업체가, 때로는 소매업체가, 때로는 플랫폼이 그 역할을 맡습니다.

segments.src: **Channel conflict** shows up in three shapes:
segments.tr: **채널 갈등(Channel conflict)**은 세 가지 형태로 나타납니다:

segments.src: 1. **Vertical conflict** — between different levels. Brand vs. retailer over price, terms, or shelf space.
segments.tr: 1. **수직적 갈등(Vertical conflict)** — 서로 다른 단계 간의 갈등입니다. 가격, 조건, 매대 공간을 두고 브랜드와 소매업체가 대립하는 경우입니다.

segments.src: 2. **Horizontal conflict** — between players at the same level. Two franchisees of the same chain fighting over an overlapping trade area.
segments.tr: 2. **수평적 갈등(Horizontal conflict)** — 동일한 단계에 있는 주체들 간의 갈등입니다. 동일한 체인의 두 가맹점이 겹치는 상권을 두고 다투는 경우입니다.

segments.src: 3. **Multichannel (or cross-channel) conflict** — the newest and loudest kind. A brand's own direct-to-consumer website competes with the very retailers who built its business.
segments.tr: 3. **다중채널(또는 교차채널) 갈등(Multichannel conflict)** — 가장 새롭고 소란스러운 형태입니다. 브랜드의 자체 D2C(Direct-to-Consumer) 웹사이트가 자신의 비즈니스를 키워준 소매업체들과 직접 경쟁하는 경우입니다.

segments.src: The usual root causes: **goal incompatibility** (the brand wants long-term brand equity, the retailer wants this weekend's traffic), **unclear roles and rights** (who owns the customer data?
segments.tr: 일반적인 근본 원인은 다음과 같습니다: **목표 불일치**(브랜드는 장기적인 브랜드 자산을 원하고, 소매업체는 이번 주말의 매출을 원함), **불명확한 역할과 권리**(고객 데이터는 누가 소유하는가?

segments.src: who eats the return?), and **differing perceptions of reality** (each side reads the same sales numbers and reaches opposite conclusions).
segments.tr: 반품 비용은 누가 부담하는가?), 그리고 **현실에 대한 인식 차이**(양측이 똑같은 매출 수치를 보고도 정반대의 결론에 도달함).

segments.src: One nuance worth keeping: not all conflict is bad.
segments.tr: 기억해 둘 만한 미묘한 차이는 모든 갈등이 나쁜 것은 아니라는 점입니다.

segments.src: Moderate, well-aired disagreement is **functional conflict** — it surfaces problems and forces better plans.
segments.tr: 적당하고 공개적으로 논의되는 의견 충돌은 **기능적 갈등(functional conflict)**입니다. 이는 문제점을 표면화하고 더 나은 계획을 수립하도록 강제합니다.

segments.src: Conflict becomes **dysfunctional** when it stops being about the issue and starts being about winning.
segments.tr: 갈등이 쟁점에 대한 논의에서 벗어나 승리 자체에 집착하기 시작할 때 **역기능적 갈등(dysfunctional)

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: It's Saturday in Columbus, Ohio, and you want a specific running shoe.
segments.tr: 오하이오주 콜럼버스의 토요일 오후, 당신은 특정 러닝화를 사고 싶어 합니다.

segments.src: The brand's own site lists it at **$140**, in an exclusive colorway you can't get anywhere else, and gives you loyalty points and free returns.
segments.tr: 브랜드의 자체 사이트에서는 이 신제품을 **$140**에 판매하고 있으며, 다른 곳에서는 구할 수 없는 단독 컬러웨이를 제공하고, 멤버십 포인트와 무료 반품 혜택까지 줍니다.

segments.src: The Foot Locker two miles away has the same silhouette — but not that colorway — also at $140, because a **MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) policy** prevents the store from advertising it any lower.
segments.tr: 2마일 떨어진 곳에 있는 풋락커 매장에도 같은 실루엣의 신제품이 있지만 그 컬러웨이는 없고 가격은 동일하게 $140입니다. 이는 **MAP(최저광고가격) 정책** 때문에 매장에서 그보다 낮게 광고할 수 없기 때문입니다.

segments.src: So you order online.
segments.tr: 그래서 당신은 온라인으로 주문합니다.

segments.src: So does everyone else.
segments.tr: 다른 사람들도 모두 그렇게 합니다.

segments.src: Now watch the conflict unfold.
segments.tr: 이제 갈등이 전개되는 과정을 지켜보세요.

segments.src: The retailer sees its best-selling brand siphoning off customers with better product and better perks, so it hands prime floor space to a rival brand and orders 30% less next season.
segments.tr: 소매업체는 베스트셀러 브랜드가 더 나은 제품과 혜택으로 고객을 빼내가고 있는 것을 보고, 경쟁 브랜드에 핵심 매장 공간을 내어주고 다음 시즌 발주량을 30% 줄입니다.

segments.src: The brand suddenly loses the discovery engine — the wall where people actually try shoes on — and its DTC growth stalls.
segments.tr: 브랜드는 갑자기 소비자가 실제로 신발을 신어보는 공간인 '발견의 엔진'을 잃게 되고, D2C 성장이 정체됩니다.

segments.src: Both sides used their power.
segments.tr: 양측 모두 자신의 파워를 사용했습니다.

segments.src: Both sides lost.
segments.tr: 그리고 양측 모두 패배했습니다.

segments.src: This isn't hypothetical.
segments.tr: 이것은 가상의 이야기가 아닙니다.

segments.src: Over the last decade several major athletic and apparel brands pulled sharply back from wholesale to go direct, then spent the following years rebuilding those same retail relationships after discovering that stores drive discovery, trial, and reach that a website can't replicate.
segments.tr: 지난 10년 동안 여러 주요 운동복 및 의류 브랜드가 도매 채널에서 대거 철수하여 직영으로 전환했다가, 웹사이트만으로는 흉내낼 수 없는 오프라인 매장만의 발견, 체험, 도달 효과를 매장들이 만들어낸다는 사실을 깨닫고는 이후 몇 년간 다시 그 유통 관계를 복원하느라 애를 먹었습니다.

segments.src: What a well-managed version looks like: **channel-specific assortments** (exclusive colorways for the store, too, not just the site), **shared inventory and sell-through data** so both sides forecast off the same numbers, **buy-online-pick-up-in-store** where the store gets credit for the sale, and a **joint business plan** signed once a year that states what each side owes the other.
segments.tr: 잘 관리된 버전의 모습은 다음과 같습니다: **채널별 구색**(사이트뿐만 아니라 매장만을 위한 단독 컬러웨이 제공), **공유 재고 및 판매 데이터**를 통해 양측이 동일한 수치를 바탕으로 수요를 예측, 매장이 판매 실적을 인정받는 **온라인 주문 후 매장 픽업(BOPIS)**, 그리고 각 측이 상대에게 무엇을 제공해야 하는지 명시한 연 1회의 **공동 사업 계획(joint business plan)** 체결.

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: 똑같은 두 회사, 똑같은 파워, 완전히 다른 결과.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. 유통 채널은 서로 상충하는 목표를 가진 독립된 기업들로 구성되어 있으므로 갈등은 성격의 문제가 아니라 구조적인 문제입니다.

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. 파워는 보상, 강압, 합법성, 전문성, 준거에서 비롯되며 양방향으로 흐르기 때문에, 파워에만 의존하면 보복을 부르게 됩니다.

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. 지속 가능한 해결책은 파트너십입니다. 공동의 목표, 명확한 역할, 공유된 데이터, 그리고 협력이 승리하는 것보다 더 이익이 되도록 만드는 정렬된 인센티브가 필요합니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** A shoe brand's own website and the department store that carries it compete for the same shopper.
segments.tr: **1.** 신발 브랜드의 자체 웹사이트와 그 제품을 취급하는 백화점이 동일한 쇼퍼를 두고 경쟁하고 있습니다.

segments.src: What type of conflict is this?
segments.tr: 이러한 갈등은 어떤 유형인가요?

segments.src: A) Horizontal conflict
segments.tr: A) 수평적 갈등

segments.src: B) Vertical conflict
segments.tr: B) 수직적 갈등

segments.src: C) Multichannel (cross-channel) conflict
segments.tr: C) 다중채널(교차채널) 갈등

segments.src: D) Functional conflict
segments.tr: D) 기능적 갈등

segments.src: **2.** A supplier tells a retailer: "Miss your volume target and we'll cut your allocation next season."
segments.tr: **2.** 공급업체가 소매업체에게 말합니다: "볼륨 목표를 달성하지 못하면 다음 시즌 할당량을 깎겠습니다."

segments.src: Which source of power is being used?
segments.tr: 어떤 파워의 원천이 사용되고 있나요?

segments.src: A) Referent power
segments.tr: A) 준거적 파워

segments.src: B) Coercive power
segments.tr: B) 강압적 파워

segments.src: C) Expert power
segments.tr: C) 전문적 파워

segments.src: D) Legitimate power
segments.tr: D) 합법적 파워

segments.src: **3.** **O / X** — All channel conflict is harmful and should be eliminated.
segments.tr: **3.** **O / X** — 모든 채널 갈등은 해로으므로 반드시 없애야 한다.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The set of independent firms that move a product from producer to final customer.
segments.tr: - **유통 채널(Distribution channel)** — 제품을 생산자에서 최종 소비자에게 이동시키는 독립된 기업들의 집합.

segments.src: - **Channel power** — One member's ability to influence another's decisions, rooted in the other party's dependence.
segments.tr: - **채널 파워(Channel power)** — 상대방의 의존성에 기반하여, 한 구성원이 다른 구성원의 의정에 영향을 미칠 수 있는 능력.

segments.src: - **Channel captain** — The member with enough power and capability to coordinate the channel's overall strategy.
segments.tr: - **채널 리더(Channel captain)** — 채널의 전체 전략을 조율할 수 있는 충분한 파워와 역량을 갖춘 구성원.

segments.src: - **Multichannel conflict** — Friction that arises when a supplier sells through its own direct channel and through third-party retailers at the same time.
segments.tr: - **다중채널 갈등(Multichannel conflict)** — 공급업체가 자체 직영 채널과 제3자 소매 채널을 통해 동시에 판매할 때 발생하는 마찰.

segments.src: - **Superordinate goal** — A shared objective bigger than either party's individual interest (e.g., growing total category demand), used to defuse conflict.
segments.tr: - **상위 목표(Superordinate goal)** — 갈등을 해소하기 위해 사용되는, 어느 한쪽의 개별 이익보다 더 큰 공동의 목표(예: 전체 카테고리 수요 성장).

segments.src: - **Vertical marketing system (VMS)** — A channel deliberately unified by ownership, contract, or one member's power, designed to reduce conflict by design rather than by negotiation.
segments.tr: - **수직적 마케팅 시스템(Vertical marketing system, VMS)** — 협상이 아니라 설계에 의해 갈등을 줄이기 위해 소유권, 계약, 또는 한 구성원의 파워로 의도적으로 통합된 채널.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) C** — the conflict is between a supplier's direct channel and its retail partners serving the same shopper, which is multichannel conflict; it's also vertical in structure, but "multichannel" is the precise term for the DTC-vs-wholesale case.
segments.tr: *정답: **1) C** — 공급업체의 직영 채널과 동일한 쇼퍼를 응대하는 소매 파트너 간의 갈등이므로 다중채널 갈등입니다. 구조적으로는 수직적이기도 하지만, DTC 대 도매의 경우에 가장 정확한 용어는 '다중채널'입니다.

segments.src: **2) B** — withholding supply or allocation is a penalty, which is coercive power (a promise of better terms would be reward power).
segments.tr: **2) B** — 공급이나 물량 배정을 보류하는 것은 처벌에 해당하며, 이는 강압적 파워입니다(더 나은 조건을 약속하는 것은 보상적 파워에 해당합니다).

segments.src: **3) X** — moderate, openly managed conflict is functional: it surfaces real problems and pushes both sides toward better plans.

zh.title: [零售学基础 #3] 为什么你喜爱的品牌和销售它的店铺正在悄悄打仗

segments.src: > Every distribution channel runs on power, and wherever there's power there's conflict — the partnerships that win are the ones that turn a tug-of-war into a shared plan.
segments.tr: > 每个分销渠道都靠权力运转，只要有权力的地方就有冲突——能赢得合作的往往是那些把拉锯战变成共同计划的伙伴。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: A product almost never travels straight from a factory to your hands.
segments.tr: 一件产品几乎从不直接从工厂送到你手里。

segments.src: It passes through a **distribution channel**: manufacturer → distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: 它要经过一个**分销渠道**：制造商 → 分销商 → 零售商 → 你。

segments.src: Each link is a separate company with its own P&L, its own boss, and its own definition of a good quarter.
segments.tr: 每一个环节都是一个独立的实体，有自己的损益表、自己的老板，以及对好季度的不同定义。

segments.src: They need each other, but they don't want the same things.
segments.tr: 他们彼此需要，但诉求并不一致。

segments.src: That gap is where **channel power** comes in.
segments.tr: **渠道权力**的概念便由此产生。

segments.src: The simplest way to think about it:
segments.tr: 最简单的理解方式：

segments.src: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you
segments.tr: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you

segments.src: ÷ how easily they could replace you
segments.tr: ÷ how easily they could replace you

segments.src: Retail textbooks usually break power into five sources (adapted from French and Raven's classic framework):
segments.tr: 零售学教材通常将权力分为五种来源（改编自 French 和 Raven 的经典框架）：

segments.src: - **Reward power** — "Hit this volume and you get better terms, co-op ad dollars, early access to the new line."
segments.tr: - **奖励权力**（Reward power）——“达到这个销量，你就能获得更好的条款、联合广告资金、以及优先获得新品系列的机会。”

segments.src: - **Coercive power** — "Miss the target and we cut your allocation, delay shipments, or give the endcap to someone else."
segments.tr: - **强制权力**（Coercive power）——“没达到目标，我们就削减你的货品配额、延迟发货，或者把端架让给别人。”

segments.src: - **Legitimate power** — "The contract says so." Rights spelled out in a franchise agreement or supply deal.
segments.tr: - **法定权力**（Legitimate power）——“合同上是这么写的。”特许经营协议或供应协议中明确规定的权利。

segments.src: - **Expert power** — "We know this category better than you do." Category-management data, merchandising know-how, demand forecasts.
segments.tr: - **专家权力**（Expert power）——“我们比你更懂这个品类。”品类管理数据、陈列专业知识、需求预测。

segments.src: - **Referent power** — "People want to be associated with us." A brand so desirable that retailers compete to carry it.
segments.tr: - **参照权力**（Referent power）——“人们渴望与我们产生关联。”一个让零售商争相代理的极具吸引力的品牌。

segments.src: Notice that power flows **both directions**.
segments.tr: 请注意，权力的流动是**双向的**。

segments.src: A national brand has expert and referent power; a large chain has reward and coercive power because it controls shelf space and traffic.
segments.tr: 全国性品牌拥有专家权和参照权；大型连锁企业则拥有奖励权和强制权，因为它们控制着货架空间和客流量。

segments.src: Neither side is automatically the boss.
segments.tr: 没有哪一方自动就是老大。

segments.src: The party that effectively coordinates the channel is called the **channel captain** — sometimes the manufacturer, sometimes the retailer, sometimes a platform.
segments.tr: 能够有效协调渠道的一方被称为**渠道主导者**（或渠道领袖，Channel captain）——有时是制造商，有时是零售商，有时则是平台。

segments.src: **Channel conflict** shows up in three shapes:
segments.tr: **渠道冲突**表现为三种形式：

segments.src: 1. **Vertical conflict** — between different levels. Brand vs. retailer over price, terms, or shelf space.
segments.tr: 1. **垂直冲突**——发生在不同层级之间。品牌与零售商之间关于价格、条款或货架空间的争夺。

segments.src: 2. **Horizontal conflict** — between players at the same level. Two franchisees of the same chain fighting over an overlapping trade area.
segments.tr: 2. **水平冲突**——发生在同一层级的参与者之间。同一连锁店的两个加盟商在重叠的贸易区内竞争。

segments.src: 3. **Multichannel (or cross-channel) conflict** — the newest and loudest kind. A brand's own direct-to-consumer website competes with the very retailers who built its business.
segments.tr: 3. **多渠道（或跨渠道）冲突**——最新也是最喧嚣的一种。品牌自有的直接面向消费者（DTC）网站，正与那些帮它建立起业务的零售商展开竞争。

segments.src: The usual root causes: **goal incompatibility** (the brand wants long-term brand equity, the retailer wants this weekend's traffic), **unclear roles and rights** (who owns the customer data?
segments.tr: 常见的根源包括：**目标不相容**（品牌想要长期的品牌资产，零售商想要这个周末的客流量）、**角色与权利不清**（谁拥有客户数据？

segments.src: who eats the return?), and **differing perceptions of reality** (each side reads the same sales numbers and reaches opposite conclusions).
segments.tr: 谁承担退货成本？），以及**对现实看法的差异**（双方阅读同样的销售数据却得出相反的结论）。

segments.src: One nuance worth keeping: not all conflict is bad.
segments.tr: 有一个细微差别值得记住：并非所有冲突都是坏事。

segments.src: Moderate, well-aired disagreement is **functional conflict** — it surfaces problems and forces better plans.
segments.tr: 适度的、充分表达的分歧属于**功能性冲突**——它能暴露出问题并促成更好的计划。

segments.src: Conflict becomes **dysfunctional** when it stops being about the issue and starts being about winning.
segments.tr: 当冲突不再围绕问题本身，而是变成为了“赢”而争时，它就变成了** dysfunctional 冲突**（功能失调的冲突）。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: It's Saturday in Columbus, Ohio, and you want a specific running shoe.
segments.tr: 这是俄亥俄州哥伦布市的一个星期六，你想要一双特定的跑步鞋。

segments.src: The brand's own site lists it at **$140**, in an exclusive colorway you can't get anywhere else, and gives you loyalty points and free returns.
segments.tr: 该品牌的官网上标价为 **$140**，采用别处买不到的独家配色，还赠送积分和免费退货服务。

segments.src: The Foot Locker two miles away has the same silhouette — but not that colorway — also at $140, because a **MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) policy** prevents the store from advertising it any lower.
segments.tr: 两英里外的 Foot Locker 也有同样的鞋型——但没有那个配色——售价同样是 $140，因为**最低广告价格（MAP）政策**限制了该店不能以更低的价格进行宣传。

segments.src: So you order online.
segments.tr: 于是你在网上订购了。

segments.src: So does everyone else.
segments.tr: 其他人也是如此。

segments.src: Now watch the conflict unfold.
segments.tr: 现在来看冲突是如何展开的。

segments.src: The retailer sees its best-selling brand siphoning off customers with better product and better perks, so it hands prime floor space to a rival brand and orders 30% less next season.
segments.tr: 零售商发现其最畅销的品牌正以更好的产品和福利分流客户，于是它把黄金铺位分给了竞争品牌，并在下一季度少订了 30% 的货。

segments.src: The brand suddenly loses the discovery engine — the wall where people actually try shoes on — and its DTC growth stalls.
segments.tr: 该品牌突然失去了发现引擎——那个让人们真正试穿鞋子的实体墙面——其 DTC 业务增长也随之停滞。

segments.src: Both sides used their power.
segments.tr: 双方都使用了各自的权力。

segments.src: Both sides lost.
segments.tr: 双方都输了。

segments.src: This isn't hypothetical.
segments.tr: 这并非假设。

segments.src: Over the last decade several major athletic and apparel brands pulled sharply back from wholesale to go direct, then spent the following years rebuilding those same retail relationships after discovering that stores drive discovery, trial, and reach that a website can't replicate.
segments.tr: 在过去的十年里，几家主要的运动和服饰品牌大幅缩减批发业务转而做直销，随后却花了好几年时间重新修复这些零售关系，因为他们发现，网站无法复制实体店所能带来的发现、试穿和触达能力。

segments.src: What a well-managed version looks like: **channel-specific assortments** (exclusive colorways for the store, too, not just the site), **shared inventory and sell-through data** so both sides forecast off the same numbers, **buy-online-pick-up-in-store** where the store gets credit for the sale, and a **joint business plan** signed once a year that states what each side owes the other.
segments.tr: 管理良好的版本看起来是这样的：**渠道专属的产品组合**（不仅官网上有，实体店也有独家配色）、**共享库存和动销数据**以便双方根据相同的数据进行预测、**线上下单门店自提**（由门店记入销售业绩），以及一份每年签署一次的**联合商业计划**，规定双方各自对彼此承担的责任。

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: 同样的两家公司，同样的权力，却带来了完全不同的结果。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. 分销渠道由目标冲突的独立企业组成，因此冲突是结构性的，而不是性格问题。

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. 权力来自奖励、强制、法定、专业和参照——且权力是双向流动的，因此单单依仗权力只会招致报复。

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. 持久的解决方案是合作：共同的目标、清晰的角色、共享的数据以及对齐的激励机制，让合作比单纯的赢更有利可图。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自我测验

segments.src: **1.** A shoe brand's own website and the department store that carries it compete for the same shopper.
segments.tr: **1.** 某鞋类品牌的自有网站与销售该鞋的百货商店在争夺同一位消费者。

segments.src: What type of conflict is this?
segments.tr: 这是什么类型的冲突？

segments.src: A) Horizontal conflict
segments.tr: A) 水平冲突

segments.src: B) Vertical conflict
segments.tr: B) 垂直冲突

segments.src: C) Multichannel (cross-channel) conflict
segments.tr: C) 多渠道（跨渠道）冲突

segments.src: D) Functional conflict
segments.tr: D) 功能性冲突

segments.src: **2.** A supplier tells a retailer: "Miss your volume target and we'll cut your allocation next season."
segments.tr: **2.** 供应商对零售商说：“如果达不到销售目标，我们将在下个季度削减你的配额。”

segments.src: Which source of power is being used?
segments.tr: 这里使用的是哪种权力来源？

segments.src: A) Referent power
segments.tr: A) 参照权力

segments.src: B) Coercive power
segments.tr: B) 强制权力

segments.src: C) Expert power
segments.tr: C) 专家权力

segments.src: D) Legitimate power
segments.tr: D) 法定权力

segments.src: **3.** **O / X** — All channel conflict is harmful and should be eliminated.
segments.tr: **3.** **对 / 错（O / X）** — 所有的渠道冲突都是有害的，应当被彻底消除。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The set of independent firms that move a product from producer to final customer.
segments.tr: - **分销渠道**（Distribution channel）——将产品从生产商转移到最终客户的一组独立企业。

segments.src: - **Channel power** — One member's ability to influence another's decisions, rooted in the other party's dependence.
segments.tr: - **渠道权力**（Channel power）——渠道成员影响另一个成员决策的能力，根植于另一方的依赖性。

segments.src: - **Channel captain** — The member with enough power and capability to coordinate the channel's overall strategy.
segments.tr: - **渠道主导者**（Channel captain）——具备足够权力和能力来协调渠道整体战略的成员。

segments.src: - **Multichannel conflict** — Friction that arises when a supplier sells through its own direct channel and through third-party retailers at the same time.
segments.tr: - **多渠道冲突**（Multichannel conflict）——当供应商同时通过自有直销渠道和第三方零售商进行销售时所产生的摩擦。

segments.src: - **Superordinate goal** — A shared objective bigger than either party's individual interest (e.g., growing total category demand), used to defuse conflict.
segments.tr: - **超协调目标**（Superordinate goal）——大于任何一方单方面利益的共同目标（例如：扩大整个品类的需求），用于化解冲突。

segments.src: - **Vertical marketing system (VMS)** — A channel deliberately unified by ownership, contract, or one member's power, designed to reduce conflict by design rather than by negotiation.
segments.tr: - **垂直营销系统（VMS）**——通过所有权、契约或某一成员的权力有意统合起来的渠道，旨在从设计上而非通过谈判来减少冲突。

segments.src: *Answers: **1) C** — the conflict is between a supplier's direct channel and its retail partners serving the same shopper, which is multichannel conflict; it's also vertical in structure, but "multichannel" is the precise term for the DTC-vs-wholesale case.
segments.tr: *答案：**1) C** — 冲突发生在供应商的直销渠道与其服务同一消费者的零售合作伙伴之间，属于多渠道冲突；从结构上看它也是垂直的，但“多渠道”是针对 DTC 对阵批发情况的精确术语。

segments.src: **2) B** — withholding supply or allocation is a penalty, which is coercive power (a promise of better terms would be reward power).
segments.tr: **2) B** — 扣留供应或配额是一种惩罚，属于强制权力（承诺提供更好的条款则是奖励权力）。

segments.src: **3) X** — moderate, openly managed conflict is functional: it surfaces real problems and pushes both sides toward better plans.
segments.tr: **3) X** — 适度的、公开管理的冲突是功能性的：它能浮现出真正的问题，并推动双方走向更好的计划。

segments.src: Only dysfunctional conflict, where the goal shifts from solving the issue to beating the partner, needs to be shut down.*
segments.tr: 只有当目标从解决问题转变为击败合作伙伴的、功能失调的冲突，才需要被叫停。*

segments.tr: ध्यान दें कि शक्ति **दोनों दिशाओं** में प्रवाहित होती है।

segments.src: A national brand has expert and referent power; a large chain has reward and coercive power because it controls shelf space and traffic.
segments.tr: एक राष्ट्रीय ब्रांड के पास विशेषज्ञ और संदर्भित शक्ति होती है; एक बड़ी श्रृंखला के पास इनाम और जबरदस्ती की शक्ति होती है क्योंकि यह शेल्फ स्पेस और ट्रैफ़िक को नियंत्रित करती है।

segments.src: Neither side is automatically the boss.
segments.tr: कोई भी पक्ष स्वचालित रूप से बॉस नहीं है।

segments.src: The party that effectively coordinates the channel is called the **channel captain** — sometimes the manufacturer, sometimes the retailer, sometimes a platform.
segments.tr: चैनल का प्रभावी ढंग से समन्वय करने वाले दल को **चैनल कप्तान** कहा जाता है — कभी-कभी निर्माता, कभी-कभी खुदरा विक्रेता, कभी-कभी एक मंच।

segments.src: **Channel conflict** shows up in three shapes:
segments.tr: **चैनल संघर्ष** तीन रूपों में दिखाई देता है:

segments.src: 1. **Vertical conflict** — between different levels. Brand vs. retailer over price, terms, or shelf space.
segments.tr: 1. **वर्टिकल संघर्ष** — विभिन्न स्तरों के बीच। मूल्य, शर्तों या शेल्फ स्पेस पर ब्रांड बनाम खुदरा विक्रेता।

segments.src: 2. **Horizontal conflict** — between players at the same level. Two franchisees of the same chain fighting over an overlapping trade area.
segments.tr: 2. **हॉरिजॉन्टल संघर्ष** — एक ही स्तर पर खिलाड़ियों के बीच। एक ही श्रृंखला के दो फ्रेंचाइजी एक ओवरलैपिंग व्यापार क्षेत्र पर लड़ रहे हैं।

segments.src: 3. **Multichannel (or cross-channel) conflict** — the newest and loudest kind. A brand's own direct-to-consumer website competes with the very retailers who built its business.
segments.tr: 3. **मल्टीचैनल (या क्रॉस-चैनल) संघर्ष** — सबसे नया और सबसे मुखर प्रकार। एक ब्रांड की अपनी डायरेक्ट-टू-consumer वेबसाइट उन खुदरा विक्रेताओं के साथ प्रतिस्पर्धा करती है जिन्होंने अपना व्यवसाय बनाया है।

segments.src: The usual root causes: **goal incompatibility** (the brand wants long-term brand equity, the retailer wants this weekend's traffic), **unclear roles and rights** (who owns the customer data?
segments.tr: सामान्य मूल कारण: **लक्ष्य असंगति** (ब्रांड दीर्घकालिक ब्रांड इक्विटी चाहता है, खुदरा विक्रेता इस सप्ताहांत का ट्रैफ़िक चाहता है), **अस्पष्ट भूमिकाएँ और अधिकार** (ग्राहक डेटा का मालिक कौन है?

segments.src: who eats the return?), and **differing perceptions of reality** (each side reads the same sales numbers and reaches opposite conclusions).
segments.tr: वापसी कौन खाता है?), और **वास्तविकता की अलग-अलग धारणाएं** (प्रत्येक पक्ष एक ही बिक्री संख्या को पढ़ता है और विपरीत निष्कर्ष पर पहुंचता है)।

segments.src: One nuance worth keeping: not all conflict is bad.
segments.tr: रखने लायक एक सूक्ष्मता: सारा संघर्ष बुरा नहीं है।

segments.src: Moderate, well-aired disagreement is **functional conflict** — it surfaces problems and forces better plans.
segments.tr: मध्यम, अच्छी तरह से प्रसारित असहमति **फंक्शनल संघर्ष** है — यह समस्याओं को सतह पर लाता है और बेहतर योजनाओं को मजबूर करता है।

segments.src: Conflict becomes **dysfunctional** when it stops being about the issue and starts being about winning.
segments.tr: संघर्ष **डिसफंक्शनल** हो जाता है जब यह मुद्दे के बारे में होना बंद हो जाता है और जीतने के बारे में होने लगता है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: It's Saturday in Columbus, Ohio, and you want a specific running shoe.
segments.tr: कोलंबस, ओहियो में शनिवार है, और आप एक विशिष्ट रनिंग जूता चाहते हैं।

segments.src: The brand's own site lists it at **$140**, in an exclusive colorway you can't get anywhere else, and gives you loyalty points and free returns.
segments.tr: ब्रांड की अपनी साइट इसे **$140** पर सूचीबद्ध करती है, एक विशेष कलरवे में जो आपको कहीं और नहीं मिल सकता है, और आपको लॉयल्टी पॉइंट और मुफ्त रिटर्न देती है।

segments.src: The Foot Locker two miles away has the same silhouette — but not that colorway — also at $140, because a **MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) policy** prevents the store from advertising it any lower.
segments.tr: दो मील की दूरी पर फुट लॉकर में वही सिल्हूट है - लेकिन वह कलरवे नहीं है - $140 पर भी, क्योंकि एक **MAP (न्यूनतम विज्ञापित मूल्य) नीति** स्टोर को इसे किसी भी कम विज्ञापित करने से रोकती है।

segments.src: So you order online.
segments.tr: तो आप ऑनलाइन ऑर्डर करते हैं।

segments.src: So does everyone else.
segments.tr: बाकी सब भी ऐसा ही करते हैं।

segments.src: Now watch the conflict unfold.
segments.tr: अब संघर्ष को सामने आते हुए देखें।

segments.src: The retailer sees its best-selling brand siphoning off customers with better product and better perks, so it hands prime floor space to a rival brand and orders 30% less next season.
segments.tr: खुदरा विक्रेता अपने सबसे अधिक बिकने वाले ब्रांड को बेहतर उत्पाद और बेहतर पर्क के साथ ग्राहकों को दूर ले जाते हुए देखता है, इसलिए यह एक प्रतिद्वंद्वी ब्रांड को प्रमुख मंजिल स्थान सौंपता है और अगली सीज़न में 30% कम ऑर्डर करता है।

segments.src: The brand suddenly loses the discovery engine — the wall where people actually try shoes on — and its DTC growth stalls.
segments.tr: ब्रांड अचानक डिस्कवरी इंजन को खो देता है — वह दीवार जहाँ लोग वास्तव में जूते आज़माते हैं — और इसकी DTC वृद्धि रुक जाती है।

segments.src: Both sides used their power.
segments.tr: दोनों पक्षों ने अपनी शक्ति का इस्तेमाल किया।

segments.src: Both sides lost.
segments.tr: दोनों पक्ष हार गए।

segments.src: This isn't hypothetical.
segments.tr: यह काल्पनिक नहीं है।

segments.src: Over the last decade several major athletic and apparel brands pulled sharply back from wholesale to go direct, then spent the following years rebuilding those same retail relationships after discovering that stores drive discovery, trial, and reach that a website can't replicate.
segments.tr: पिछले दशक में कई प्रमुख एथलेटिक और परिधान ब्रांड सीधे जाने के लिए थोक से पीछे हट गए, फिर यह पता लगाने के बाद कि स्टोर डिस्कवरी, परीक्षण और पहुंच को चलाते हैं जिसे एक वेबसाइट दोहरा नहीं सकती है, उन समान खुदरा संबंधों को फिर से बनाने में अगले साल बिताए।

segments.src: What a well-managed version looks like: **channel-specific assortments** (exclusive colorways for the store, too, not just the site), **shared inventory and sell-through data** so both sides forecast off the same numbers, **buy-online-pick-up-in-store** where the store gets credit for the sale, and a **joint business plan** signed once a year that states what each side owes the other.
segments.tr: एक अच्छी तरह से प्रबंधित संस्करण कैसा दिखता है: **चैनल-विशिष्ट वर्गीकरण** (स्टोर के लिए विशेष कलरवे, केवल साइट के लिए नहीं), **साझा इन्वेंट्री और सेल-थ्रू डेटा** ताकि दोनों पक्ष एक ही नंबरों से पूर्वानुमान लगाएं, **बाय-ऑनलाइन-पिक-अप-इन-स्टोर** जहां स्टोर को बिक्री का श्रेय मिलता है, और एक **संयुक्त व्यापार योजना** साल में एक बार हस्ताक्षर की जाती है जो बताती है कि प्रत्येक पक्ष दूसरे का क्या ऋणी है।

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: वही दो कंपनियां, वही शक्ति, पूरी तरह से अलग परिणाम।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## थ्री-लाइन सारांश

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. वितरण चैनल परस्पर विरोधी लक्ष्यों वाली स्वतंत्र फर्मों से बने होते हैं, इसलिए संघर्ष संरचनात्मक है, कोई व्यक्तित्व समस्या नहीं है।

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. शक्ति इनाम, जबरदस्ती, वैधता, विशेषज्ञता और संदर्भ से आती है — और यह दोनों दिशाओं में प्रवाहित होती है, इसलिए इस पर अकेले झुकना प्रतिशोध को आमंत्रित करता है।

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. टिकाऊ समाधान साझेदारी है: साझा लक्ष्य, स्पष्ट भूमिकाएँ, साझा डेटा और संरेखित प्रोत्साहन जो सहयोग को जीतने की तुलना में अधिक लाभदायक बनाते हैं।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व-प्रोत्साहन

segments.src: **1.** A shoe brand's own website and the department store that carries it compete for the same shopper.
segments.tr: **1.** एक जूता ब्रांड की अपनी वेबसाइट और उसे ले जाने वाला डिपार्टमेंट स्टोर एक ही खरीदार के लिए प्रतिस्पर्धा करते हैं।

segments.src: What type of conflict is this?
segments.tr: यह किस प्रकार का संघर्ष है?

segments.src: A) Horizontal conflict
segments.tr: A) हॉरिजॉन्टल संघर्ष

segments.src: B) Vertical conflict
segments.tr: B) वर्टिकल संघर्ष

segments.src: C) Multichannel (cross-channel) conflict
segments.tr: C) मल्टीचैनल (क्रॉस-चैनल) संघर्ष

segments.src: D) Functional conflict
segments.tr: D) फंक्शनल संघर्ष

segments.src: **2.** A supplier tells a retailer: "Miss your volume target and we'll cut your allocation next season."
segments.tr: **2.** एक आपूर्तिकर्ता एक खुदरा विक्रेता से कहता है: "अपने वॉल्यूम लक्ष्य से चूक जाइए और हम अगले सीज़न में आपका आवंटन काट देंगे।"

segments.src: Which source of power is being used?
segments.tr: शक्ति के किस स्रोत का उपयोग किया जा रहा है?

segments.src: A) Referent power
segments.tr: A) रेफरेंट पावर

segments.src: B) Coercive power
segments.tr: B) कोर्सिव पावर

segments.src: C) Expert power
segments.tr: C) एक्सपर्ट पावर

segments.src: D) Legitimate power
segments.tr: D) लेजिस्मेट पावर

segments.src: **3.** **O / X** — All channel conflict is harmful and should be eliminated.
segments.tr: **3.** **O / X** — सभी चैनल संघर्ष हानिकारक हैं और उन्हें समाप्त किया जाना चाहिए।

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The set of independent firms that move a product from producer to final customer.
segments.tr: - **डिस्ट्रिब्यूशन चैनल** — स्वतंत्र फर्मों का सेट जो उत्पाद को निर्माता से अंतिम ग्राहक तक ले जाता है।

segments.src: - **Channel power** — One member's ability to influence another's decisions, rooted in the other party's dependence.
segments.tr: - **चैनल पावर** — दूसरे के निर्णयों को प्रभावित करने की एक सदस्य की क्षमता, दूसरे पक्ष की निर्भरता में निहित है।

segments.src: - **Channel captain** — The member with enough power and capability to coordinate the channel's overall strategy.
segments.tr: - **चैनल कप्तान** — चैनल की समग्र रणनीति का समन्वय करने के लिए पर्याप्त शक्ति और क्षमता वाला सदस्य।

segments.src: - **Multichannel conflict** — Friction that arises when a supplier sells through its own direct channel and through third-party retailers at the same time.
segments.tr: - **मल्टीचैनल संघर्ष** — घर्षण जो तब उत्पन्न होता है जब कोई आपूर्तिकर्ता अपने स्वयं के प्रत्यक्ष चैनल के माध्यम से और उसी समय तीसरे पक्ष के खुदरा विक्रेताओं के माध्यम से बेचता है।

segments.src: - **Superordinate goal** — A shared objective bigger than either party's individual interest (e.g., growing total category demand), used to defuse conflict.
segments.tr: - **सुपरऑर्डिनेट गोल** — संघर्ष को कम करने के लिए उपयोग किया जाने वाला किसी भी पार्टी के व्यक्तिगत हित से बड़ा एक साझा उद्देश्य (उदा., कुल श्रेणी की मांग बढ़ाना)।

segments.src: - **Vertical marketing system (VMS)** — A channel deliberately unified by ownership, contract, or one member's power, designed to reduce conflict by design rather than by negotiation.
segments.tr: - **वर्टिकल मार्केटिंग सिस्टम (VMS)** — बातचीत के बजाय डिजाइन द्वारा संघर्ष को कम करने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया स्वामित्व, अनुबंध या एक सदस्य की शक्ति द्वारा जानबूझकर एकीकृत चैनल।

segments.src: *Answers: **1) C** — the conflict is between a supplier's direct channel and its retail partners serving the same shopper, which is multichannel conflict; it's also vertical in structure, but "multichannel" is the precise term for the DTC-vs-wholesale case.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **1) C** — संघर्ष एक आपूर्तिकर्ता के प्रत्यक्ष चैनल और उसके खुदरा भागीदारों के बीच है जो एक ही खरीदार की सेवा करते हैं, जो मल्टीचैनल संघर्ष है; यह संरचना में वर्टिकल भी है, लेकिन "मल्टीचैनल" DTC-बनाम-थोक मामले के लिए सटीक शब्द है।

segments.src: **2) B** — withholding supply or allocation is a penalty, which is coercive power (a promise of better terms would be reward power).
segments.tr: **2) B** — आपूर्ति या आवंटन को रोकना एक दंड है, जो कोर्सिव पावर है (बेहतर शर्तों का वादा रिवार्ड पावर होगा)।

segments.src: **3) X** — moderate, openly managed conflict is functional: it surfaces real problems and pushes both sides toward better plans.
segments.tr: **3) X** — मध्यम, खुले तौर पर प्रबंधित संघर्ष कार्यात्मक है: यह वास्तविक समस्याओं को सतह पर लाता है और दोनों पक्षों को बेहतर योजनाओं की ओर धकेलता है।

segments.src: Only dysfunctional conflict, where the goal shifts from solving the issue to beating the partner, needs to be shut down.*
segments.tr: केवल डिस्फंक्शनल संघर्ष, जहां लक्ष्य मुद्दे को हल करने से बदलकर साथी को हराने के लिए स्थानांतरित हो जाता है, को बंद करने की आवश्यकता है।*

es.title: [Retailing 101 #3] Por qué tu marca favorita y la tienda que la vende están peleando silenciosamente

segments.src: > Every distribution channel runs on power, and wherever there's power there's conflict — the partnerships that win are the ones that turn a tug-of-war into a shared plan.
segments.tr: > Cada canal de distribución funciona con poder, y donde hay poder hay conflicto: las asociaciones que ganan son las que convierten un tira y afloja en un plan compartido.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: A product almost never travels straight from a factory to your hands.
segments.tr: Un producto casi nunca viaja directamente de una fábrica a tus manos.

segments.src: It passes through a **distribution channel**: manufacturer → distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: Pasa a través de un **canal de distribución**: fabricante → distribuidor → minorista → tú.

segments.src: Each link is a separate company with its own P&L, its own boss, and its own definition of a good quarter.
segments.tr: Cada eslabón es una empresa separada con su propio P&L, su propio jefe y su propia definición de un buen trimestre.

segments.src: They need each other, but they don't want the same things.
segments.tr: Se necesitan mutuamente, pero no quieren las mismas cosas.

segments.src: That gap is where **channel power** comes in.
segments.tr: Esa brecha es donde entra el **poder de canal**.

segments.src: The simplest way to think about it:
segments.tr: La forma más sencilla de pensarlo:

segments.src: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you
segments.tr: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you

segments.src: ÷ how easily they could replace you
segments.tr: ÷ how easily they could replace you

segments.src: Retail textbooks usually break power into five sources (adapted from French and Raven's classic framework):
segments.tr: Los libros de texto de venta minorista generalmente dividen el poder en cinco fuentes (adaptadas del marco clásico de French y Raven):

segments.src: - **Reward power** — "Hit this volume and you get better terms, co-op ad dollars, early access to the new line."
segments.tr: - **Poder de recompensa** — "Alcanza este volumen y obtendrás mejores condiciones, dólares para publicidad cooperativa, acceso anticipado a la nueva línea."

segments.src: - **Coercive power** — "Miss the target and we cut your allocation, delay shipments, or give the endcap to someone else."
segments.tr: - **Poder coercitivo** — "Si no alcanzas el objetivo, reduciremos tu asignación, retrasaremos los envíos o le daremos el espacio de exhibición a alguien más."

segments.src: - **Legitimate power** — "The contract says so." Rights spelled out in a franchise agreement or supply deal.
segments.tr: - **Poder legítimo** — "El contrato lo dice". Derechos detallados en un acuerdo de franquicia o contrato de suministro.

segments.src: - **Expert power** — "We know this category better than you do." Category-management data, merchandising know-how, demand forecasts.
segments.tr: - **Poder de experto** — "Conocemos esta categoría mejor que tú". Datos de gestión de categorías, conocimientos de merchandising, pronósticos de demanda.

segments.src: - **Referent power** — "People want to be associated with us." A brand so desirable that retailers compete to carry it.
segments.tr: - **Poder de referente** — "La gente quiere ser asociada con nosotros". Una marca tan deseable que los minoristas compiten por venderla.

segments.src: Notice that power flows **both directions**.
segments.tr: Nota que el poder fluye en **ambas direcciones**.

segments.src: A national brand has expert and referent power; a large chain has reward and coercive power because it controls shelf space and traffic.
segments.tr: Una marca nacional tiene poder de experto y de referente; una gran cadena tiene poder de recompensa y coercitivo porque controla el espacio en estantería y el tráfico.

segments.src: Neither side is automatically the boss.
segments.tr: Ninguno de los dos lados es automáticamente el jefe.

segments.src: The party that effectively coordinates the channel is called the **channel captain** — sometimes the manufacturer, sometimes the retailer, sometimes a platform.
segments.tr: La parte que coordina eficazmente el canal se llama **capitán de canal**: a veces el fabricante, a veces el minorista, a veces una plataforma.

segments.src: **Channel conflict** shows up in three shapes:
segments.tr: **Conflicto de canal** se manifiesta de tres formas:

segments.src: 1. **Vertical conflict** — between different levels. Brand vs. retailer over price, terms, or shelf space.
segments.tr: 1. **Conflicto vertical** — entre diferentes niveles. Marca vs. minorista sobre precio, términos o espacio en estantería.

segments.src: 2. **Horizontal conflict** — between players at the same level. Two franchisees of the same chain fighting over an overlapping trade area.
segments.tr: 2. **Conflicto horizontal** — entre jugadores al mismo nivel. Dos franquiciados de la misma cadena peleando por un área comercial superpuesta.

segments.src: 3. **Multichannel (or cross-channel) conflict** — the newest and loudest kind. A brand's own direct-to-consumer website competes with the very retailers who built its business.
segments.tr: 3. **Conflicto multicanal (o intercanal)** — el tipo más nuevo y ruidoso. El sitio web directo al consumidor de una marca compite con los mismos minoristas que construyeron su negocio.

segments.src: The usual root causes: **goal incompatibility** (the brand wants long-term brand equity, the retailer wants this weekend's traffic), **unclear roles and rights** (who owns the customer data?
segments.tr: Las causas raíz habituales: **incompatibilidad de objetivos** (la marca quiere valor de marca a largo plazo, el minorista quiere el tráfico de este fin de semana), **roles y derechos poco claros** (¿quién posee los datos del cliente?

segments.src: who eats the return?), and **differing perceptions of reality** (each side reads the same sales numbers and reaches opposite conclusions).
segments.tr: ¿quién absorbe las devoluciones?), y **diferentes percepciones de la realidad** (cada lado lee los mismos números de ventas y llega a conclusiones opuestas).

segments.src: One nuance worth keeping: not all conflict is bad.
segments.tr: Un matiz que vale la pena mantener: no todo conflicto es malo.

segments.src: Moderate, well-aired disagreement is **functional conflict** — it surfaces problems and forces better plans.
segments.tr: El desacuerdo moderado y bien expresado es un **conflicto funcional**: saca a la luz problemas y fuerza mejores planes.

segments.src: Conflict becomes **dysfunctional** when it stops being about the issue and starts being about winning.
segments.tr: El conflicto se vuelve **disfuncional** cuando deja de tratarse del problema y empieza a tratarse de ganar.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: It's Saturday in Columbus, Ohio, and you want a specific running shoe.
segments.tr: Es sábado en Columbus, Ohio, y quieres un zapato de correr específico.

segments.src: The brand's own site lists it at **$140**, in an exclusive colorway you can't get anywhere else, and gives you loyalty points and free returns.
segments.tr: El sitio de la propia marca lo lista a **$140**, en una combinación de colores exclusiva que no puedes conseguir en ningún otro lugar, y te da puntos de lealtad y devoluciones gratuitas.

segments.src: The Foot Locker two miles away has the same silhouette — but not that colorway — also at $140, because a **MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) policy** prevents the store from advertising it any lower.
segments.tr: El Foot Locker a dos millas de distancia tiene la misma silueta —pero no esa combinación de colores— también a $140, porque una **política de MAP (Precio Mínimo Anunciado)** impide que la tienda lo anuncie a un precio menor.

segments.src: So you order online.
segments.tr: Así que pides en línea.

segments.src: So does everyone else.
segments.tr: También lo hace todo el mundo.

segments.src: Now watch the conflict unfold.
segments.tr: Ahora observa cómo se desarrolla el conflicto.

segments.src: The retailer sees its best-selling brand siphoning off customers with better product and better perks, so it hands prime floor space to a rival brand and orders 30% less next season.
segments.tr: El minorista ve que su marca más vendida le quita clientes con mejores productos y mejores beneficios, así que le da el espacio principal en el piso a una marca rival y pide un 30% menos la próxima temporada.

segments.src: The brand suddenly loses the discovery engine — the wall where people actually try shoes on — and its DTC growth stalls.
segments.tr: La marca pierde repentinamente el motor de descubrimiento —la pared donde la gente realmente se prueba los zapatos— y su crecimiento DTC se estanca.

segments.src: Both sides used their power.
segments.tr: Ambos lados usaron su poder.

segments.src: Both sides lost.
segments.tr: Ambos lados perdieron.

segments.src: This isn't hypothetical.
segments.tr: Esto no es hipotético.

segments.src: Over the last decade several major athletic and apparel brands pulled sharply back from wholesale to go direct, then spent the following years rebuilding those same retail relationships after discovering that stores drive discovery, trial, and reach that a website can't replicate.
segments.tr: Durante la última década, varias marcas importantes de atletismo y ropa se retiraron bruscamente de la venta al por mayor para ir directo al consumidor, luego pasaron los años siguientes reconstruyendo esas mismas relaciones minoristas después de descubrir que las tiendas impulsan el descubrimiento, la prueba y el alcance que un sitio web no puede replicar.

segments.src: What a well-managed version looks like: **channel-specific assortments** (exclusive colorways for the store, too, not just the site), **shared inventory and sell-through data** so both sides forecast off the same numbers, **buy-online-pick-up-in-store** where the store gets credit for the sale, and a **joint business plan** signed once a year that states what each side owes the other.
segments.tr: Cómo se ve una versión bien gestionada: **surtidos específicos por canal** (combinaciones de colores exclusivas para la tienda también, no solo para el sitio), **inventario compartido y datos de ventas** para que ambos lados pronostiquen con los mismos números, **comprar en línea y recoger en tienda** donde la tienda recibe crédito por la venta, y un **plan de negocios conjunto** firmado una vez al año que establece lo que cada lado debe al otro.

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: Las mismas dos empresas, el mismo poder, un resultado completamente diferente.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen de tres líneas

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. Los canales de distribución están hechos de empresas independientes con objetivos conflictivos, por lo que el conflicto es estructural, no un problema de personalidad.

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. El poder proviene de la recompensa, la coerción, la legitimidad, la experiencia y la referencia, y fluye en ambas direcciones, por lo que apoyarse solo en él invita a represalias.

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. La solución duradera es la asociación: objetivos compartidos, roles claros, datos compartidos e incentivos alineados que hacen que la cooperación sea más rentable que ganar.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The set of independent firms that move a product from producer to final customer.
segments.tr: - **Canal de distribución** — El conjunto de empresas independientes que mueven un producto desde el productor hasta el cliente final.

segments.src: - **Channel power** — One member's ability to influence another's decisions, rooted in the other party's dependence.
segments.tr: - **Poder de canal** — La capacidad de un miembro para influir en las decisiones de otro, arraigada en la dependencia de la otra parte.

segments.src: - **Channel captain** — The member with enough power and capability to coordinate the channel's overall strategy.
segments.tr: - **Capitán de canal** — El miembro con suficiente poder y capacidad para coordinar la estrategia general del canal.

segments.src: - **Multichannel conflict** — Friction that arises when a supplier sells through its own direct channel and through third-party retailers at the same time.
segments.tr: - **Conflicto multicanal** — Fricción que surge cuando un proveedor vende a través de su propio canal directo y a través de minoristas externos al mismo tiempo.

segments.src: - **Superordinate goal** — A shared objective bigger than either party's individual interest (e.g., growing total category demand), used to defuse conflict.
segments.tr: - **Objetivo supraordenado** — Un objetivo compartido más grande que el interés individual de cualquiera de las partes (por ejemplo, aumentar la demanda total de la categoría), utilizado para desactivar el conflicto.

segments.src: - **Vertical marketing system (VMS)** — A channel deliberately unified by ownership, contract, or one member's power, designed to reduce conflict by design rather than by negotiation.
segments.tr: - **Sistema de marketing vertical (VMS)** — Un canal deliberadamente unificado por propiedad, contrato o el poder de un miembro, diseñado para reducir el conflicto por diseño en lugar de por negociación.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) C** — the conflict is between a supplier's direct channel and its retail partners serving the same shopper, which is multichannel conflict; it's also vertical in structure, but "multichannel" is the precise term for the DTC-vs-wholesale case.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **1) C** — el conflicto es entre el canal directo de un proveedor y sus socios minoristas que atienden al mismo comprador, lo cual es conflicto multicanal; también es vertical en estructura, pero "multicanal" es el término preciso para el caso de DTC vs. venta al por mayor.

segments.src: **2) B** — withholding supply or allocation is a penalty, which is coercive power (a promise of better terms would be reward power).
segments.tr: **2) B** — retener el suministro o la asignación es una penalización, lo cual es poder coercitivo (una promesa de mejores términos sería poder de recompensa).

segments.src: **3) X** — moderate, openly managed conflict is functional: it surfaces real problems and pushes both sides toward better plans.
segments.tr: **3) X** — el conflicto moderado y gestionado abiertamente es funcional: saca a la luz problemas reales y empuja a ambos lados hacia mejores planes.

segments.src: Only dysfunctional conflict, where the goal shifts from solving the issue to beating the partner, needs to be shut down.*
segments.tr: Solo el conflicto disfuncional, donde el objetivo cambia de resolver el problema a vencer al socio, necesita ser detenido.*

segments.src: That gap is where **channel power** comes in.

fr.title: [Retailing 101 #3] Pourquoi votre marque préférée et le magasin qui la vend se livrent une guerre silencieuse

segments.src: > Every distribution channel runs on power, and wherever there's power there's conflict — the partnerships that win are the ones that turn a tug-of-war into a shared plan.
segments.tr: > Chaque canal de distribution repose sur le pouvoir, et partout où il y a du pouvoir, il y a des conflits — les partenariats qui gagnent sont ceux qui transforment un bras de fer en plan partagé.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept du jour

segments.src: A product almost never travels straight from a factory to your hands.
segments.tr: Un produit ne vapresque jamais directement d'une usine à vos mains.

segments.src: It passes through a **distribution channel**: manufacturer → distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: Il passe par un **canal de distribution** : fabricant → distributeur → détaillant → vous.

segments.src: Each link is a separate company with its own P&L, its own boss, and its own definition of a good quarter.
segments.tr: Chaque maillon est une entreprise distincte avec son propre compte de résultat, son propre patron et sa propre définition d'un bon trimestre.

segments.src: They need each other, but they don't want the same things.
segments.tr: Ils ont besoin les uns des autres, mais ils ne veulent pas la même chose.

segments.src: That gap is where **channel power** comes in.
segments.tr: C'est dans cet écart que réside le **pouvoir de canal**.

segments.src: The simplest way to think about it:
segments.tr: La façon la plus simple de l'envisager :

segments.src: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you
segments.tr: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you

segments.src: ÷ how easily they could replace you
segments.tr: ÷ how easily they could replace you

segments.src: Retail textbooks usually break power into five sources (adapted from French and Raven's classic framework):
segments.tr: Les manuels de vente au détail divisent généralement le pouvoir en cinq sources (adaptées du cadre classique de French et Raven) :

segments.src: - **Reward power** — "Hit this volume and you get better terms, co-op ad dollars, early access to the new line."
segments.tr: - **Pouvoir de récompense** — "Atteignez ce volume et vous obtiendrez de meilleures conditions, des fonds publicitaires coopératifs, un accès anticipé à la nouvelle ligne."

segments.src: - **Coercive power** — "Miss the target and we cut your allocation, delay shipments, or give the endcap to someone else."
segments.tr: - **Pouvoir de coercition** — "Manquez l'objectif et nous réduirons votre allocation, retarderons les expéditions ou donnerons la tête de gondole à quelqu'un d'autre."

segments.src: - **Legitimate power** — "The contract says so." Rights spelled out in a franchise agreement or supply deal.
segments.tr: - **Pouvoir légitime** — "Le contrat le dit." Droits énoncés dans un accord de franchise ou un contrat d'approvisionnement.

segments.src: - **Expert power** — "We know this category better than you do." Category-management data, merchandising know-how, demand forecasts.
segments.tr: - **Pouvoir d'expertise** — "Nous connaissons cette catégorie mieux que vous." Données de gestion de catégorie, savoir-faire en matière de marchandisage, prévisions de la demande.

segments.src: - **Referent power** — "People want to be associated with us." A brand so desirable that retailers compete to carry it.
segments.tr: - **Pouvoir de référence** — "Les gens veulent être associés à nous." Une marque si désirable que les détaillants se disputent pour la distribuer.

segments.src: Notice that power flows **both directions**.
segments.tr: Remarquez que le pouvoir circule **dans les deux sens**.

segments.src: A national brand has expert and referent power; a large chain has reward and coercive power because it controls shelf space and traffic.
segments.tr: Une marque nationale a un pouvoir d'expertise et de référence ; une grande chaîne a un pouvoir de récompense et de coercition parce qu'elle contrôle l'espace de vente et le trafic.

segments.src: Neither side is automatically the boss.
segments.tr: Aucun des deux camps n'est automatiquement le chef.

segments.src: The party that effectively coordinates the channel is called the **channel captain** — sometimes the manufacturer, sometimes the retailer, sometimes a platform.
segments.tr: La partie qui coordonne efficacement le canal est appelée le **chef de file du canal** — parfois le fabricant, parfois le détaillant, parfois une plateforme.

segments.src: **Channel conflict** shows up in three shapes:
segments.tr: Le **conflit de canal** se manifeste sous trois formes :

segments.src: 1. **Vertical conflict** — between different levels. Brand vs. retailer over price, terms, or shelf space.
segments.tr: 1. **Conflit vertical** — entre différents niveaux. Marque contre détaillant sur le prix, les conditions ou l'espace en rayon.

segments.src: 2. **Horizontal conflict** — between players at the same level. Two franchisees of the same chain fighting over an overlapping trade area.
segments.tr: 2. **Conflit horizontal** — entre acteurs du même niveau. Deux franchisés de la même chaîne se disputant une zone de chalandise qui se chevauche.

segments.src: 3. **Multichannel (or cross-channel) conflict** — the newest and loudest kind. A brand's own direct-to-consumer website competes with the very retailers who built its business.
segments.tr: 3. **Conflit multicanal (ou intercanal)** — le type le plus récent et le plus bruyant. Le propre site direct-to-consumer d'une marque concurrence les détaillants mêmes qui ont bâti son activité.

segments.src: The usual root causes: **goal incompatibility** (the brand wants long-term brand equity, the retailer wants this weekend's traffic), **unclear roles and rights** (who owns the customer data?
segments.tr: Les causes profondes habituelles : **l'incompatibilité des objectifs** (la marque veut une valeur de marque à long terme, le détaillant veut le trafic de ce week-end), **les rôles et droits flous** (à qui appartiennent les données clients ?

segments.src: who eats the return?), and **differing perceptions of reality** (each side reads the same sales numbers and reaches opposite conclusions).
segments.tr: qui prend en charge les retours ?), et **les perceptions divergentes de la réalité** (chaque camp lit les mêmes chiffres de ventes et tire des conclusions opposées).

segments.src: One nuance worth keeping: not all conflict is bad.
segments.tr: Une nuance à garder en tête : tous les conflits ne sont pas mauvais.

segments.src: Moderate, well-aired disagreement is **functional conflict** — it surfaces problems and forces better plans.
segments.tr: Un désaccord modéré et bien exprimé est un **conflit fonctionnel** — il fait surface les problèmes et force de meilleurs plans.

segments.src: Conflict becomes **dysfunctional** when it stops being about the issue and starts being about winning.
segments.tr: Le conflit devient **dysfonctionnel** lorsqu'il cesse de porter sur le problème pour se concentrer sur la victoire.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie de tous les jours

segments.src: It's Saturday in Columbus, Ohio, and you want a specific running shoe.
segments.tr: C'est samedi à Columbus, dans l'Ohio, et vous voulez une chaussure de course spécifique.

segments.src: The brand's own site lists it at **$140**, in an exclusive colorway you can't get anywhere else, and gives you loyalty points and free returns.
segments.tr: Le propre site de la marque l'affiche à **$140**, dans un coloris exclusif que vous ne trouverez nulle part ailleurs, et vous offre des points de fidélité ainsi que des retours gratuits.

segments.src: The Foot Locker two miles away has the same silhouette — but not that colorway — also at $140, because a **MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) policy** prevents the store from advertising it any lower.
segments.tr: Le Foot Locker à deux miles de là a la même silhouette — mais pas ce coloris — également à $140, car une **politique de prix publicitaire minimum (MAP)** empêche le magasin de l'annoncer à un prix inférieur.

segments.src: So you order online.
segments.tr: Vous commandez donc en ligne.

segments.src: So does everyone else.
segments.tr: Tout le monde fait de même.

segments.src: Now watch the conflict unfold.
segments.tr: Regardez maintenant le conflit se dérouler.

segments.src: The retailer sees its best-selling brand siphoning off customers with better product and better perks, so it hands prime floor space to a rival brand and orders 30% less next season.
segments.tr: Le détaillant voit sa marque la plus vendue siphonner ses clients avec un meilleur produit et de meilleurs avantages, il attribue donc un espace de premier choix à une marque rivale et commande 30 % de moins la saison prochaine.

segments.src: The brand suddenly loses the discovery engine — the wall where people actually try shoes on — and its DTC growth stalls.
segments.tr: La marque perd soudainement le moteur de découverte — le mur où les gens essaient réellement les chaussures — et sa croissance DTC stagne.

segments.src: Both sides used their power.
segments.tr: Les deux camps ont utilisé leur pouvoir.

segments.src: Both sides lost.
segments.tr: Les deux camps ont perdu.

segments.src: This isn't hypothetical.
segments.tr: Ce n'est pas hypothétique.

segments.src: Over the last decade several major athletic and apparel brands pulled sharply back from wholesale to go direct, then spent the following years rebuilding those same retail relationships after discovering that stores drive discovery, trial, and reach that a website can't replicate.
segments.tr: Au cours de la dernière décennie, plusieurs grandes marques d'athlétisme et de vêtements ont fortement réduit la vente en gros pour passer au direct, puis ont passé les années suivantes à reconstruire ces mêmes relations de vente au détail après avoir découvert que les magasins stimulent la découverte, l'essai et la portée qu'un site Web ne peut pas reproduire.

segments.src: What a well-managed version looks like: **channel-specific assortments** (exclusive colorways for the store, too, not just the site), **shared inventory and sell-through data** so both sides forecast off the same numbers, **buy-online-pick-up-in-store** where the store gets credit for the sale, and a **joint business plan** signed once a year that states what each side owes the other.
segments.tr: À quoi ressemble une version bien gérée : des **assortiments spécifiques au canal** (des coloris exclusifs pour le magasin aussi, pas seulement pour le site), **des données partagées sur les stocks et les ventes** afin que les deux parties prévoient sur les mêmes chiffres, **l'achat en ligne avec retrait en magasin** où le magasin obtient le crédit de la vente, et un **plan d'affaires conjoint** signé une fois par an qui indique ce que chaque partie doit à l'autre.

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: Mêmes deux entreprises, même pouvoir, résultat complètement différent.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Résumé en trois lignes

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. Les canaux de distribution sont constitués d'entreprises indépendantes aux objectifs contradictoires, de sorte que le conflit est structurel, et non un problème de personnalité.

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. Le pouvoir provient de la récompense, de la coercition, de la légitimité, de l'expertise et de la référence — et il circule dans les deux sens, de sorte que s'y fier seul invite aux représailles.

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. La solution durable est le partenariat : des objectifs partagés, des rôles clairs, des données partagées et des incitations alignées qui rendent la coopération plus rentable que la victoire.
