pt.title: [Varejo 101 #3] Por que sua marca favorita e a loja que a vende estão silenciosamente em conflito

segments.src: > Every distribution channel runs on power, and wherever there's power there's conflict — the partnerships that win are the ones that turn a tug-of-war into a shared plan.
segments.tr: > Todo canal de distribuição funciona baseado em poder, e onde há poder há conflito — as parcerias que ganham são as que transformam um cabo de guerra em um plano compartilhado.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: A product almost never travels straight from a factory to your hands.
segments.tr: Um produto quase nunca viaja diretamente de uma fábrica para suas mãos.

segments.src: It passes through a **distribution channel**: manufacturer → distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: Ele passa por um **canal de distribuição**: fabricante → distribuidor → varejista → você.

segments.src: Each link is a separate company with its own P&L, its own boss, and its own definition of a good quarter.
segments.tr: Cada elo é uma empresa separada com seu próprio DRE, seu próprio chefe e sua própria definição de um bom trimestre.

segments.src: They need each other, but they don't want the same things.
segments.tr: Eles precisam um do outro, mas não querem as mesmas coisas.

segments.src: That gap is where **channel power** comes in.
segments.tr: Essa lacuna é onde o **poder do canal** entra em cena.

segments.src: The simplest way to think about it:
segments.tr: A forma mais simples de pensar sobre isso:

segments.src: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you
segments.tr: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you

segments.src: ÷ how easily they could replace you
segments.tr: ÷ how easily they could replace you

segments.src: Retail textbooks usually break power into five sources (adapted from French and Raven's classic framework):
segments.tr: Livros didáticos de varejo geralmente dividem o poder em cinco fontes (adaptado do marco clássico de French e Raven):

segments.src: - **Reward power** — "Hit this volume and you get better terms, co-op ad dollars, early access to the new line."
segments.tr: - **Poder de recompensa** — "Atinja este volume e você obtém melhores termos, dólares de anúncios cooperativos, acesso antecipado à nova linha."

segments.src: - **Coercive power** — "Miss the target and we cut your allocation, delay shipments, or give the endcap to someone else."
segments.tr: - **Poder coercitivo** — "Perca o alvo e reduzimos sua alocação, atrasamos envios ou damos o endcap para outra pessoa."

segments.src: - **Legitimate power** — "The contract says so." Rights spelled out in a franchise agreement or supply deal.
segments.tr: - **Poder legítimo** — "O contrato diz assim." Direitos especificados em um acordo de franquia ou contrato de fornecimento.

segments.src: - **Expert power** — "We know this category better than you do." Category-management data, merchandising know-how, demand forecasts.
segments.tr: - **Poder de especialista** — "Conhecemos essa categoria melhor do que você." Dados de gerenciamento de categoria, conhecimento de merchandising, previsões de demanda.

segments.src: - **Referent power** — "People want to be associated with us." A brand so desirable that retailers compete to carry it.
segments.tr: - **Poder referencial** — "As pessoas querem estar associadas a nós." Uma marca tão desejável que varejistas competem para carregá-la.

segments.src: Notice that power flows **both directions**.
segments.tr: Observe que o poder flui em **ambas as direções**.

segments.src: A national brand has expert and referent power; a large chain has reward and coercive power because it controls shelf space and traffic.
segments.tr: Uma marca nacional tem poder de especialista e referencial; uma grande rede tem poder de recompensa e coercitivo porque controla o espaço de prateleira e o tráfego.

segments.src: Neither side is automatically the boss.
segments.tr: Nenhum lado é automaticamente o chefe.

segments.src: The party that effectively coordinates the channel is called the **channel captain** — sometimes the manufacturer, sometimes the retailer, sometimes a platform.
segments.tr: A parte que coordena efetivamente o canal é chamada de **capitão do canal** — às vezes o fabricante, às vezes o varejista, às vezes uma plataforma.

segments.src: **Channel conflict** shows up in three shapes:
segments.tr: **Conflito de canal** aparece em três formas:

segments.src: 1. **Vertical conflict** — between different levels. Brand vs. retailer over price, terms, or shelf space.
segments.tr: 1. **Conflito vertical** — entre diferentes níveis. Marca versus varejista sobre preço, termos ou espaço de prateleira.

segments.src: 2. **Horizontal conflict** — between players at the same level. Two franchisees of the same chain fighting over an overlapping trade area.
segments.tr: 2. **Conflito horizontal** — entre jogadores no mesmo nível. Dois franqueados da mesma rede lutando por uma área comercial sobreposta.

segments.src: 3. **Multichannel (or cross-channel) conflict** — the newest and loudest kind. A brand's own direct-to-consumer website competes with the very retailers who built its business.
segments.tr: 3. **Conflito multicanal (ou entre canais)** — o tipo mais novo e mais alto. O próprio site direto-ao-consumidor de uma marca compete com os mesmos varejistas que construíram seu negócio.

segments.src: The usual root causes: **goal incompatibility** (the brand wants long-term brand equity, the retailer wants this weekend's traffic), **unclear roles and rights** (who owns the customer data?
segments.tr: As causas raiz usuais: **incompatibilidade de objetivos** (a marca quer patrimônio de marca de longo prazo, o varejista quer o tráfego deste fim de semana), **papéis e direitos pouco claros** (quem é o proprietário dos dados do cliente?

segments.src: who eats the return?), and **differing perceptions of reality** (each side reads the same sales numbers and reaches opposite conclusions).
segments.tr: quem absorve a devolução?), e **percepções diferentes da realidade** (cada lado lê os mesmos números de vendas e chega a conclusões opostas).

segments.src: One nuance worth keeping: not all conflict is bad.
segments.tr: Uma nuance que vale a pena manter: nem todo conflito é ruim.

segments.src: Moderate, well-aired disagreement is **functional conflict** — it surfaces problems and forces better plans.
segments.tr: Desacordo moderado e bem discutido é **conflito funcional** — ele traz à tona problemas e força planos melhores.

segments.src: Conflict becomes **dysfunctional** when it stops being about the issue and starts being about winning.
segments.tr: O conflito se torna **disfuncional** quando para de ser sobre o problema e começa a ser sobre ganhar.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: It's Saturday in Columbus, Ohio, and you want a specific running shoe.
segments.tr: É sábado em Columbus, Ohio, e você quer um tênis de corrida específico.

segments.src: The brand's own site lists it at **$140**, in an exclusive colorway you can't get anywhere else, and gives you loyalty points and free returns.
segments.tr: O próprio site da marca o lista por **$140**, em um colorway exclusivo que você não consegue em nenhum outro lugar, e oferece pontos de fidelidade e devoluções gratuitas.

segments.src: The Foot Locker two miles away has the same silhouette — but not that colorway — also at $140, because a **MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) policy** prevents the store from advertising it any lower.
segments.tr: A Foot Locker a dois quilômetros de distância tem a mesma silhueta — mas não esse colorway — também por $140, porque uma **política MAP (Preço Mínimo Anunciado)** impede a loja de anunciá-lo mais baixo.

segments.src: So you order online.
segments.tr: Então você faz um pedido online.

segments.src: So does everyone else.
segments.tr: Assim como todo mundo.

segments.src: Now watch the conflict unfold.
segments.tr: Agora observe o conflito se desenrolar.

segments.src: The retailer sees its best-selling brand siphoning off customers with better product and better perks, so it hands prime floor space to a rival brand and orders 30% less next season.
segments.tr: O varejista vê sua marca mais vendida desviando clientes com produto melhor e melhores benefícios, então entrega o espaço de chão principal para uma marca rival e pede 30% menos na próxima temporada.

segments.src: The brand suddenly loses the discovery engine — the wall where people actually try shoes on — and its DTC growth stalls.
segments.tr: A marca de repente perde o mecanismo de descoberta — a parede onde as pessoas realmente experimentam sapatos — e seu crescimento direto ao consumidor estagna.

segments.src: Both sides used their power.
segments.tr: Ambos os lados usaram seu poder.

segments.src: Both sides lost.
segments.tr: Ambos os lados perderam.

segments.src: This isn't hypothetical.
segments.tr: Isso não é hipotético.

segments.src: Over the last decade several major athletic and apparel brands pulled sharply back from wholesale to go direct, then spent the following years rebuilding those same retail relationships after discovering that stores drive discovery, trial, and reach that a website can't replicate.
segments.tr: Na última década, várias grandes marcas de atletismo e vestuário se afastaram drasticamente do atacado para ir direto, e então passaram os anos seguintes reconstruindo essas mesmas relações de varejo depois de descobrir que as lojas impulsionam a descoberta, a experimentação e o alcance que um site não consegue replicar.

segments.src: What a well-managed version looks like: **channel-specific assortments** (exclusive colorways for the store, too, not just the site), **shared inventory and sell-through data** so both sides forecast off the same numbers, **buy-online-pick-up-in-store** where the store gets credit for the sale, and a **joint business plan** signed once a year that states what each side owes the other.
segments.tr: Como é uma versão bem gerenciada: **sortimentos específicos do canal** (colorways exclusivos para a loja também, não apenas para o site), **dados de inventário e venda compartilhados** para que ambos os lados façam previsões a partir dos mesmos números, **comprar online e buscar na loja** onde a loja recebe crédito pela venda, e um **plano de negócios conjunto** assinado uma vez por ano que indica o que cada lado deve ao outro.

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: Mesmas duas empresas, mesmo poder, resultado completamente diferente.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumo em Três Linhas

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. Os canais de distribuição são compostos por empresas independentes com objetivos conflitantes, portanto o conflito é estrutural, não um problema de personalidade.

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. O poder vem da recompensa, coerção, legitimidade, expertise e referência — e flui em ambas as direções, portanto confiar apenas nele convida à retaliação.

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. A solução durável é a parceria: objetivos compartilhados, papéis claros, dados compartilhados e incentivos alinhados que tornam a cooperação mais lucrativa do que vencer.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Auto-Teste

segments.src: **1.** A shoe brand's own website and the department store that carries it compete for the same shopper.
segments.tr: **1.** O próprio site de uma marca de sapato e a loja de departamentos que a carrega competem pelo mesmo comprador.

segments.src: What type of conflict is this?
segments.tr: Que tipo de conflito é este?

segments.src: A) Horizontal conflict
segments.tr: A) Conflito horizontal

segments.src: B) Vertical conflict
segments.tr: B) Conflito vertical

segments.src: C) Multichannel (cross-channel) conflict
segments.tr: C) Conflito multicanal (entre canais)

segments.src: D) Functional conflict
segments.tr: D) Conflito funcional

segments.src: **2.** A supplier tells a retailer: "Miss your volume target and we'll cut your allocation next season."
segments.tr: **2.** Um fornecedor diz a um varejista: "Perca seu alvo de volume e reduziremos sua alocação na próxima temporada."

segments.src: Which source of power is being used?
segments.tr: Qual fonte de poder está sendo usada?

segments.src: A) Referent power
segments.tr: A) Poder referencial

segments.src: B) Coercive power
segments.tr: B) Poder coercitivo

segments.src: C) Expert power
segments.tr: C) Poder de especialista

segments.src: D) Legitimate power
segments.tr: D) Poder legítimo

segments.src: **3.** **O / X** — All channel conflict is harmful and should be eliminated.
segments.tr: **3.** **O / X** — Todo conflito de canal é prejudicial e deve ser eliminado.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The set of independent firms that move a product from producer to final customer.
segments.tr: - **Canal de distribuição** — O conjunto de empresas independentes que movem um produto do produtor para o cliente final.

segments.src: - **Channel power** — One member's ability to influence another's decisions, rooted in the other party's dependence.
segments.tr: - **Poder do canal** — A capacidade de um membro influenciar as decisões de outro, enraizada na dependência da outra parte.

segments.src: - **Channel captain** — The member with enough power and capability to coordinate the channel's overall strategy.
segments.tr: - **Capitão do canal** — O membro com poder suficiente e capacidade para coordenar a estratégia geral do canal.

segments.src: - **Multichannel conflict** — Friction that arises when a supplier sells through its own direct channel and through third-party retailers at the same time.
segments.tr: - **Conflito multicanal** — Atrito que surge quando um fornecedor vende através de seu próprio canal direto e através de varejistas de terceiros ao mesmo tempo.

segments.src: - **Superordinate goal** — A shared objective bigger than either party's individual interest (e.g., growing total category demand), used to defuse conflict.
segments.tr: - **Objetivo superordenado** — Um objetivo compartilhado maior que o interesse individual de qualquer uma das partes (por exemplo, aumentar a demanda total da categoria), usado para defusar o conflito.

segments.src: - **Vertical marketing system (VMS)** — A channel deliberately unified by ownership, contract, or one member's power, designed to reduce conflict by design rather than by negotiation.
segments.tr: - **Sistema de marketing vertical (VMS)** — Um canal deliberadamente unificado por propriedade, contrato ou poder de um membro, projetado para reduzir o conflito por design em vez de por negociação.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) C** — the conflict is between a supplier's direct channel and its retail partners serving the same shopper, which is multichannel conflict; it's also vertical in structure, but "multichannel" is the precise term for the DTC-vs-wholesale case.
segments.tr: *Respostas: **1) C** — o conflito é entre o canal direto de um fornecedor e seus parceiros de varejo servindo o mesmo comprador, o que é conflito multicanal; também é vertical em estrutura, mas "multicanal" é o termo preciso para o caso DTC vs atacado.

segments.src: **2) B** — withholding supply or allocation is a penalty, which is coercive power (a promise of better terms would be reward power).
segments.tr: **2) B** — reter o fornecimento ou alocação é uma penalidade, o que é poder coercitivo (uma promessa de melhores termos seria poder de recompensa).

segments.src: **3) X** — moderate, openly managed conflict is functional: it surfaces real problems and pushes both sides toward better plans.
segments.tr: **3) X** — conflito moderado e gerenciado abertamente é funcional: ele traz à tona problemas reais e empurra ambos os lados em direção a planos melhores.

segments.src: Only dysfunctional conflict, where the goal shifts from solving the issue to beating the partner, needs to be shut down.*
segments.tr: Apenas o conflito disfuncional, onde o objetivo muda de resolver o problema para vencer o parceiro, precisa ser encerrado.*

segments.src: - **Reward power** — "Hit this volume and you get better terms, co-op ad dollars, early access to the new line."
segments.tr: - **Kekuasaan reward** — "Capai volume ini dan Anda akan mendapatkan syarat yang lebih baik, uang iklan kerja sama, akses awal ke lini baru."

segments.src: - **Coercive power** — "Miss the target and we cut your allocation, delay shipments, or give the endcap to someone else."
segments.tr: - **Kekuasaan pemaksaan** — "Lewatkan target dan kami akan memotong alokasi Anda, menunda pengiriman, atau memberikan endcap kepada orang lain."

segments.src: - **Legitimate power** — "The contract says so." Rights spelled out in a franchise agreement or supply deal.
segments.tr: - **Kekuasaan sah** — "Kontrak mengatakan demikian." Hak yang dijelaskan dalam perjanjian waralaba atau kesepakatan pasokan.

segments.src: - **Expert power** — "We know this category better than you do." Category-management data, merchandising know-how, demand forecasts.
segments.tr: - **Kekuasaan ahli** — "Kami mengerti kategori ini lebih baik dari Anda." Data manajemen kategori, pengetahuan merchandising, prakiraan permintaan.

segments.src: - **Referent power** — "People want to be associated with us." A brand so desirable that retailers compete to carry it.

segments.src: 3. **Multichannel (or cross-channel) conflict** — the newest and loudest kind. A brand's own direct-to-consumer website competes with the very retailers who built its business.

segments.tr: Seperti apa versi yang dikelola dengan baik: **seleksi khusus saluran** (warna eksklusif untuk toko juga, bukan hanya situs), **inventaris bersama dan data penjualan** sehingga kedua pihak meramalkan dari angka yang sama, **beli-online-ambil-di-toko** di mana toko mendapat kredit untuk penjualan, dan **rencana bisnis bersama** yang ditandatangani sekali setahun yang menyatakan apa yang setiap pihak berhutang kepada pihak lain.

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: Dua perusahaan yang sama, kekuasaan yang sama, hasil yang sama sekali berbeda.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. Saluran distribusi terdiri dari perusahaan independen dengan tujuan yang bertentangan, sehingga konflik bersifat struktural, bukan masalah kepribadian.

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. Kekuasaan berasal dari reward, paksaan, legitimasi, keahlian, dan referensi — dan mengalir ke dua arah, jadi mengandalkannya saja mengundang pembalasan.

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. Perbaikan yang tahan lama adalah kemitraan: tujuan bersama, peran yang jelas, data bersama, dan insentif yang selaras yang membuat kerja sama lebih menguntungkan daripada menang.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The set of independent firms that move a product from producer to final customer.
segments.tr: - **Saluran distribusi** — Sekumpulan perusahaan independen yang memindahkan produk dari produsen ke pelanggan akhir.

segments.src: - **Channel power** — One member's ability to influence another's decisions, rooted in the other party's dependence.
segments.tr: - **Kekuasaan saluran** — Kemampuan satu anggota untuk mempengaruhi keputusan anggota lain, berakar pada ketergantungan pihak lain.

segments.src: - **Channel captain** — The member with enough power and capability to coordinate the channel's overall strategy.
segments.tr: - **Kapten saluran** — Anggota dengan kekuasaan dan kemampuan yang cukup untuk mengoordinasikan strategi saluran secara keseluruhan.

segments.src: - **Multichannel conflict** — Friction that arises when a supplier sells through its own direct channel and through third-party retailers at the same time.
segments.tr: - **Konflik multisaluran** — Gesekan yang timbul ketika supplier menjual melalui saluran langsung miliknya sendiri dan melalui pengecer pihak ketiga pada saat yang bersamaan.

segments.src: - **Superordinate goal** — A shared objective bigger than either party's individual interest (e.g., growing total category demand), used to defuse conflict.
segments.tr: - **Tujuan superordinat** — Tujuan bersama yang lebih besar daripada kepentingan individual pihak mana pun (misalnya, meningkatkan permintaan kategori total), digunakan untuk membatalkan konflik.

segments.src: - **Vertical marketing system (VMS)** — A channel deliberately unified by ownership, contract, or one member's power, designed to reduce conflict by design rather than by negotiation.
segments.tr: - **Sistem pemasaran vertikal (VMS)** — Saluran yang dengan sengaja bersatu oleh kepemilikan, kontrak, atau kekuasaan satu anggota, dirancang untuk mengurangi konflik berdasarkan desain daripada negosiasi.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) C** — the conflict is between a supplier's direct channel and its retail partners serving the same shopper, which is multichannel conflict; it's also vertical in structure, but "multichannel" is the precise term for the DTC-vs-wholesale case.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **1) C** — konflik adalah antara saluran langsung supplier dan mitra ritel-nya melayani pembeli yang sama, yang merupakan konflik multisaluran; juga vertikal dalam struktur, tetapi "multisaluran" adalah istilah yang tepat untuk kasus DTC-vs-grosir.

segments.src: **2) B** — withholding supply or allocation is a penalty, which is coercive power (a promise of better terms would be reward power).
segments.tr: **2) B** — menahan pasokan atau alokasi adalah hukuman, yang merupakan kekuasaan pemaksaan (janji syarat yang lebih baik akan menjadi kekuasaan reward).

segments.src: **3) X** — moderate, openly managed conflict is functional: it surfaces real problems and pushes both sides toward better plans.
segments.tr: **3) X** — konflik yang sedang dan dikelola secara terbuka adalah fungsional: ini menemukan masalah nyata dan mendorong kedua pihak menuju rencana yang lebih baik.

segments.src: Only dysfunctional conflict, where the goal shifts from solving the issue to beating the partner, needs to be shut down.*
segments.tr: Hanya konflik disfungsional, di mana tujuan bergeser dari menyelesaikan masalah menjadi mengalahkan mitra, yang perlu ditutup.*

ja.title: [Retailing 101 #3] あなたが好むブランドと、それを扱う店舗がひそかに争っている理由

segments.src: > Every distribution channel runs on power, and wherever there's power there's conflict — the partnerships that win are the ones that turn a tug-of-war into a shared plan.
segments.tr: > すべての流通チャネルは力によって動いており、力があるところには必ず対立がある。勝利を収めるパートナーシップとは、綱引きを共有の計画に変えるものである。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 本日のコンセプト

segments.src: A product almost never travels straight from a factory to your hands.
segments.tr: 製品はほぼ直接、工場からあなたの手に届くことはありません。

segments.src: It passes through a **distribution channel**: manufacturer → distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: それは**流通チャネル**を通ります：製造業者→流通業者→小売業者→あなた。

segments.src: Each link is a separate company with its own P&L, its own boss, and its own definition of a good quarter.
segments.tr: 各段階は独自のP&L、独自のボス、独自の「良い四半期」の定義を持つ別々の企業です。

segments.src: They need each other, but they don't want the same things.
segments.tr: 彼らは互いに必要としていますが、同じものを望んでいません。

segments.src: That gap is where **channel power** comes in.
segments.tr: その隙間に**チャネルパワー**が現れます。

segments.src: The simplest way to think about it:
segments.tr: 最もシンプルな考え方は：

segments.src: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you
segments.tr: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you

segments.src: ÷ how easily they could replace you
segments.tr: ÷ how easily they could replace you

segments.src: Retail textbooks usually break power into five sources (adapted from French and Raven's classic framework):
segments.tr: 小売の教科書は通常、パワーを5つのソースに分類しています(フレンチとレイブンの古典的なフレームワークを参考)：

segments.src: - **Reward power** — "Hit this volume and you get better terms, co-op ad dollars, early access to the new line."
segments.tr: - **報酬パワー**—「このボリュームを達成すれば、より良い条件、共同広告費、新商品への早期アクセスが得られます。」

segments.src: - **Coercive power** — "Miss the target and we cut your allocation, delay shipments, or give the endcap to someone else."
segments.tr: - **強制力**—「ターゲットを逃せば、割り当てをカットします。出荷を遅延させます。エンドキャップを他の誰かに与えます。」

segments.src: - **Legitimate power** — "The contract says so." Rights spelled out in a franchise agreement or supply deal.
segments.tr: - **正当な権力**—「契約書に書いてあります。」フランチャイズ契約や供給契約に明記された権利。

segments.src: - **Expert power** — "We know this category better than you do." Category-management data, merchandising know-how, demand forecasts.
segments.tr: - **専門知識パワー**—「このカテゴリーについて、あなたより詳しく知っています。」カテゴリー管理データ、マーチャンダイジングのノウハウ、需要予測。

segments.src: - **Referent power** — "People want to be associated with us." A brand so desirable that retailers compete to carry it.
segments.tr: - **参照パワー**—「人々は私たちと関わりたいと思っています。」小売業者が扱いたいほど望まれるブランド。

segments.src: Notice that power flows **both directions**.
segments.tr: パワーが**両方向に流れる**ことに注目してください。

segments.src: A national brand has expert and referent power; a large chain has reward and coercive power because it controls shelf space and traffic.
segments.tr: ナショナルブランドは専門知識と参照パワーを持っています。大型チェーンは棚スペースとトラフィックを支配しているため、報酬パワーと強制力を持っています。

segments.src: Neither side is automatically the boss.
segments.tr: どちら側も自動的にボスではありません。

segments.src: The party that effectively coordinates the channel is called the **channel captain** — sometimes the manufacturer, sometimes the retailer, sometimes a platform.
segments.tr: チャネルを効果的に調整する当事者は**チャネルキャプテン**と呼ばれます—時には製造業者、時には小売業者、時にはプラットフォーム。

segments.src: **Channel conflict** shows up in three shapes:
segments.tr: **チャネル対立**は3つの形で現れます：

segments.src: 1. **Vertical conflict** — between different levels. Brand vs. retailer over price, terms, or shelf space.
segments.tr: 1. **垂直対立**—異なるレベル間。ブランド対小売業者で、価格、条件、棚スペースについて。

segments.src: 2. **Horizontal conflict** — between players at the same level. Two franchisees of the same chain fighting over an overlapping trade area.
segments.tr: 2. **水平対立**—同じレベルのプレイヤー間。同じチェーンの2つのフランチャイズが重複する販売地域を巡って争う。

segments.src: 3. **Multichannel (or cross-channel) conflict** — the newest and loudest kind. A brand's own direct-to-consumer website competes with the very retailers who built its business.
segments.tr: 3. **マルチチャネル(またはクロスチャネル)対立**—最新で一番激しい種類。ブランド独自のD2Cウェブサイトが、そのビジネスを築いた小売業者と競合する。

segments.src: The usual root causes: **goal incompatibility** (the brand wants long-term brand equity, the retailer wants this weekend's traffic), **unclear roles and rights** (who owns the customer data?
segments.tr: 通常の根本原因：**目標の不一致**(ブランドは長期的なブランド資産を望み、小売業者は今週末のトラフィックを望む)、**役割と権利が不明瞭**(顧客データの所有者は誰ですか？

segments.src: who eats the return?), and **differing perceptions of reality** (each side reads the same sales numbers and reaches opposite conclusions).
segments.tr: 返品を誰が負担するのか？)、**現実の認識が異なる**(両側が同じ売上数字を見ても、反対の結論に達する)。

segments.src: One nuance worth keeping: not all conflict is bad.
segments.tr: 1つ重要なニュアンス：すべての対立が悪いわけではありません。

segments.src: Moderate, well-aired disagreement is **functional conflict** — it surfaces problems and forces better plans.
segments.tr: 適度で十分に議論された不一致は**機能的対立**です—問題を表面化させ、より良い計画を強制します。

segments.src: Conflict becomes **dysfunctional** when it stops being about the issue and starts being about winning.
segments.tr: 対立が**機能不全**になるのは、問題について議論することをやめて、相手に勝つことが目的になるときです。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活で

segments.src: It's Saturday in Columbus, Ohio, and you want a specific running shoe.
segments.tr: 土曜日です。オハイオ州コロンバス。あなたは特定のランニングシューズが欲しい。

segments.src: The brand's own site lists it at **$140**, in an exclusive colorway you can't get anywhere else, and gives you loyalty points and free returns.
segments.tr: ブランド独自のサイトは**$140**で売られていて、他では手に入らない限定色で、ロイヤルティポイントと無料返品が付きます。

segments.src: The Foot Locker two miles away has the same silhouette — but not that colorway — also at $140, because a **MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) policy** prevents the store from advertising it any lower.
segments.tr: 2マイル先のフットロッカーは同じ形—ただしその色ではない—やはり$140です。**MAP(最小広告価格)ポリシー**があるため、店舗はこれ以下で広告できません。

segments.src: So you order online.
segments.tr: だからオンラインで注文します。

segments.src: So does everyone else.
segments.tr: 誰もが同じです。

segments.src: Now watch the conflict unfold.
segments.tr: さあ、対立が展開する様子を見てください。

segments.src: The retailer sees its best-selling brand siphoning off customers with better product and better perks, so it hands prime floor space to a rival brand and orders 30% less next season.
segments.tr: 小売業者は、最も売れるブランドがより良い商品とより良い特典でお客さんを吸い上げるのを見ているため、一等地の棚スペースをライバルブランドに譲り、来シーズンは30%少なく発注します。

segments.src: The brand suddenly loses the discovery engine — the wall where people actually try shoes on — and its DTC growth stalls.
segments.tr: ブランドは突然、発見エンジン—人々が実際に靴を試着する壁—を失い、そのDTC成長は停止します。

segments.src: Both sides used their power.
segments.tr: 両側は力を使いました。

segments.src: Both sides lost.
segments.tr: 両側は負けました。

segments.src: This isn't hypothetical.
segments.tr: これは仮説の話ではありません。

segments.src: Over the last decade several major athletic and apparel brands pulled sharply back from wholesale to go direct, then spent the following years rebuilding those same retail relationships after discovering that stores drive discovery, trial, and reach that a website can't replicate.
segments.tr: 過去10年間、いくつかの大手アスレティック・アパレルブランドは卸売から直販へと大きく舵を切り、その後、店舗が発見、試着、ウェブサイトには複製できないリーチを推進することを発見した後、同じ小売関係の再構築に数年を費やしました。

segments.src: What a well-managed version looks like: **channel-specific assortments** (exclusive colorways for the store, too, not just the site), **shared inventory and sell-through data** so both sides forecast off the same numbers, **buy-online-pick-up-in-store** where the store gets credit for the sale, and a **joint business plan** signed once a year that states what each side owes the other.
segments.tr: よく管理されたバージョンの形：**チャネル固有の品揃え**(サイトだけでなく、店舗向けの限定色)、**共有在庫と売上データ**両側が同じ数字で予測する、**買ったオンラインで店舗受け取り**店舗が売上を得るケース、そして毎年署名された**共同事業計画**各側が相手に何を果たすべきかを明記。

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: 同じ2つの企業、同じ力、完全に異なる成果。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3行の要約

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. 流通チャネルは相互に対立する目標を持つ独立企業でできているため、対立は構造的問題であり、性格の問題ではありません。

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. パワーは報酬、強制、正当性、専門知識、参照に由来します—そしてそれは両方向に流れるため、それだけに頼ると報復を招きます。

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. 耐久的な解決策はパートナーシップです：共有された目標、明確な役割、共有データ、協力が勝利より利益になるような調整されたインセンティブ。

segments.src: > Every distribution channel runs on power, and wherever there's power there's conflict — the partnerships that win are the ones that turn a tug-of-war into a shared plan.
segments.tr: > Jeder Vertriebskanal läuft auf Macht, und überall dort, wo es Macht gibt, gibt es Konflikte — die Partnerschaften, die gewinnen, sind diejenigen, die ein Kräftemessen in einen gemeinsamen Plan umwandeln.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: A product almost never travels straight from a factory to your hands.
segments.tr: Ein Produkt reist fast nie direkt von einer Fabrik in Ihre Hände.

segments.src: It passes through a **distribution channel**: manufacturer → distributor → retailer → you.
segments.tr: Es durchläuft einen **Vertriebskanal**: Hersteller → Distributor → Einzelhandel → Sie.

segments.src: Each link is a separate company with its own P&L, its own boss, and its own definition of a good quarter.
segments.tr: Jeder Link ist ein separates Unternehmen mit eigenem P&L, eigenem Chef und eigener Definition eines guten Quartals.

segments.src: They need each other, but they don't want the same things.
segments.tr: Sie brauchen sich gegenseitig, aber sie wollen nicht dasselbe.

segments.src: That gap is where **channel power** comes in.
segments.tr: Diese Lücke ist der Ort, an dem **Kanalmacht** ins Spiel kommt.

segments.src: The simplest way to think about it:
segments.tr: Der einfachste Weg, darüber nachzudenken:

segments.src: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you
segments.tr: Your channel power = how badly your partner needs you

segments.src: ÷ how easily they could replace you
segments.tr: ÷ how easily they could replace you

segments.src: Retail textbooks usually break power into five sources (adapted from French and Raven's classic framework):
segments.tr: Einzelhandelslehrbücher teilen Macht normalerweise in fünf Quellen auf (angepasst an das klassische Framework von French und Raven):

segments.src: - **Reward power** — "Hit this volume and you get better terms, co-op ad dollars, early access to the new line."
segments.tr: - **Belohnungsmacht** — "Erreichen Sie dieses Volumen und Sie erhalten bessere Bedingungen, Werbegelder für Kooperationen, frühen Zugang zur neuen Linie."

segments.src: - **Coercive power** — "Miss the target and we cut your allocation, delay shipments, or give the endcap to someone else."
segments.tr: - **Erzwingungsmacht** — "Verfehlen Sie das Ziel und wir kürzen Ihre Zuteilung, verzögern Lieferungen oder geben das Endcap an jemand anderen."

segments.src: - **Legitimate power** — "The contract says so." Rights spelled out in a franchise agreement or supply deal.
segments.tr: - **Legitime Macht** — "Der Vertrag sagt das." Rechte, die in einer Franchisevereinbarung oder einem Liefervertrag festgehalten sind.

segments.src: - **Expert power** — "We know this category better than you do." Category-management data, merchandising know-how, demand forecasts.
segments.tr: - **Expertenmacht** — "Wir kennen diese Kategorie besser als Sie." Kategoriemanagementdaten, Merchandising-Know-how, Nachfrageprognosen.

segments.src: - **Referent power** — "People want to be associated with us." A brand so desirable that retailers compete to carry it.
segments.tr: - **Referenzmacht** — "Menschen möchten mit uns verbunden sein." Eine Marke so begehrt, dass Einzelhändler konkurrieren, um sie zu führen.

segments.src: Notice that power flows **both directions**.
segments.tr: Beachten Sie, dass Macht **in beide Richtungen** fließt.

segments.src: A national brand has expert and referent power; a large chain has reward and coercive power because it controls shelf space and traffic.
segments.tr: Eine nationale Marke hat Expertenmacht und Referenzmacht; eine große Kette hat Belohnungs- und Erzwingungsmacht, weil sie Regalplatz und Kundenverkehr kontrolliert.

segments.src: Neither side is automatically the boss.
segments.tr: Keine Seite ist automatisch der Boss.

segments.src: The party that effectively coordinates the channel is called the **channel captain** — sometimes the manufacturer, sometimes the retailer, sometimes a platform.
segments.tr: Die Partei, die den Kanal effektiv koordiniert, wird als **Kanalführer** bezeichnet — manchmal der Hersteller, manchmal der Einzelhändler, manchmal eine Plattform.

segments.src: **Channel conflict** shows up in three shapes:
segments.tr: **Kanalkonflikt** tritt in drei Formen auf:

segments.src: 1. **Vertical conflict** — between different levels. Brand vs. retailer over price, terms, or shelf space.
segments.tr: 1. **Vertikaler Konflikt** — zwischen verschiedenen Ebenen. Marke gegen Einzelhändler über Preis, Bedingungen oder Regalplatz.

segments.src: 2. **Horizontal conflict** — between players at the same level. Two franchisees of the same chain fighting over an overlapping trade area.
segments.tr: 2. **Horizontaler Konflikt** — zwischen Akteuren auf derselben Ebene. Zwei Franchisenehmer derselben Kette kämpfen um ein überlappendes Handelsgebiet.

segments.src: 3. **Multichannel (or cross-channel) conflict** — the newest and loudest kind. A brand's own direct-to-consumer website competes with the very retailers who built its business.
segments.tr: 3. **Multi-Kanal-(oder Cross-Kanal-)Konflikt** — die neueste und lauteste Art. Eine eigene Direct-to-Consumer-Website der Marke konkurriert mit genau den Einzelhändlern, die ihr Geschäft aufgebaut haben.

segments.src: The usual root causes: **goal incompatibility** (the brand wants long-term brand equity, the retailer wants this weekend's traffic), **unclear roles and rights** (who owns the customer data?
segments.tr: Die üblichen Ursachen: **Inkompatibilität der Ziele** (die Marke möchte langfristigen Markenwert, der Einzelhändler möchte diesen Wochenendverkehr), **unklar definierte Rollen und Rechte** (wem gehören die Kundendaten?

segments.src: who eats the return?), and **differing perceptions of reality** (each side reads the same sales numbers and reaches opposite conclusions).
segments.tr: wer trägt die Rücksendung?), und **unterschiedliche Realitätswahrnehmungen** (jede Seite liest die gleichen Verkaufszahlen und kommt zu entgegengesetzten Schlussfolgerungen).

segments.src: One nuance worth keeping: not all conflict is bad.
segments.tr: Eine wichtige Nuance: nicht alle Konflikte sind schlecht.

segments.src: Moderate, well-aired disagreement is **functional conflict** — it surfaces problems and forces better plans.
segments.tr: Gemäßigte, offen diskutierte Meinungsverschiedenheiten sind **funktionale Konflikte** — sie bringen Probleme ans Licht und erzwingen bessere Pläne.

segments.src: Conflict becomes **dysfunctional** when it stops being about the issue and starts being about winning.
segments.tr: Konflikte werden **dysfunktional**, wenn es nicht mehr um das Problem geht und um Gewinnen anfängt.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: It's Saturday in Columbus, Ohio, and you want a specific running shoe.
segments.tr: Es ist Samstag in Columbus, Ohio, und Sie möchten einen bestimmten Laufschuh.

segments.src: The brand's own site lists it at **$140**, in an exclusive colorway you can't get anywhere else, and gives you loyalty points and free returns.
segments.tr: Die eigene Website der Marke listet ihn zu **$140**, in einer exklusiven Farbvariante, die Sie nirgendwo sonst bekommen, und gibt Ihnen Treuepunkte und kostenlose Rücksendungen.

segments.src: The Foot Locker two miles away has the same silhouette — but not that colorway — also at $140, because a **MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) policy** prevents the store from advertising it any lower.
segments.tr: Der Foot Locker zwei Meilen entfernt hat die gleiche Silhouette — aber nicht diese Farbvariante — auch zu $140, weil eine **MAP-(Mindestbeworbener-Preis-)Richtlinie** den Shop daran hindert, ihn niedriger zu bewerben.

segments.src: So you order online.
segments.tr: Also bestellen Sie online.

segments.src: So does everyone else.
segments.tr: Das tun alle anderen auch.

segments.src: Now watch the conflict unfold.
segments.tr: Nun beobachten Sie, wie sich der Konflikt entfaltet.

segments.src: The retailer sees its best-selling brand siphoning off customers with better product and better perks, so it hands prime floor space to a rival brand and orders 30% less next season.
segments.tr: Der Einzelhändler sieht seine Bestseller-Marke Kunden mit besserem Produkt und besseren Vorteilen abfangen, also räumt er einer Konkurrenzmarke Regalmeter ein und bestellt nächste Saison 30% weniger.

segments.src: The brand suddenly loses the discovery engine — the wall where people actually try shoes on — and its DTC growth stalls.
segments.tr: Die Marke verliert plötzlich die Entdeckungs-Engine — die Wand, wo Menschen tatsächlich Schuhe anprobieren — und ihr DTC-Wachstum stagniert.

segments.src: Both sides used their power.
segments.tr: Beide Seiten nutzten ihre Macht.

segments.src: Both sides lost.
segments.tr: Beide Seiten verloren.

segments.src: This isn't hypothetical.
segments.tr: Das ist nicht hypothetisch.

segments.src: Over the last decade several major athletic and apparel brands pulled sharply back from wholesale to go direct, then spent the following years rebuilding those same retail relationships after discovering that stores drive discovery, trial, and reach that a website can't replicate.
segments.tr: In der letzten Dekade haben mehrere große Sport- und Bekleidungsmarken sich stark vom Großhandel zurückgezogen, um direkt zu gehen, und verbrachten dann die folgenden Jahre damit, genau diese Handelsbeziehungen wiederaufzubauen, nachdem sie festgestellt hatten, dass Läden Entdeckung, Ausprobieren und Reichweite antreiben, die eine Website nicht replizieren kann.

segments.src: What a well-managed version looks like: **channel-specific assortments** (exclusive colorways for the store, too, not just the site), **shared inventory and sell-through data** so both sides forecast off the same numbers, **buy-online-pick-up-in-store** where the store gets credit for the sale, and a **joint business plan** signed once a year that states what each side owes the other.
segments.tr: Wie eine gut verwaltete Version aussieht: **kanalspezifische Sortimente** (exklusive Farbvarianten auch für den Shop, nicht nur für die Website), **gemeinsame Bestands- und Verkaufsdaten**, damit beide Seiten mit den gleichen Zahlen prognostizieren, **online kaufen, im Shop abholen**, wobei der Shop das Verkaufs-Guthaben erhält, und einen **gemeinsamen Geschäftsplan**, der einmal im Jahr unterzeichnet wird und angibt, was jede Seite der anderen schuldet.

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: Gleiche zwei Unternehmen, gleiche Macht, völlig anderes Ergebnis.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Dreizeilige Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. Vertriebskanäle bestehen aus unabhängigen Unternehmen mit konkurrierenden Zielen, daher ist Konflikt strukturell, kein Persönlichkeitsproblem.

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. Macht kommt von Belohnung, Zwang, Legitimität, Expertise und Referenz — und sie fließt in beide Richtungen, also lädt es sich, sich allein darauf zu verlassen, zu Vergeltung ein.

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. Die dauerhafte Lösung ist Partnerschaft: gemeinsame Ziele, klare Rollen, gemeinsame Daten und aufeinander abgestimmte Anreize, die Zusammenarbeit profitabler machen als Gewinnen.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbst-Quiz

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Heutige Begriffe

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The set of independent firms that move a product from producer to final customer.
segments.tr: - **Vertriebskanal** — Die Menge unabhängiger Unternehmen, die ein Produkt vom Produzenten zum Endkunden transportieren.

segments.src: - **Channel power** — One member's ability to influence another's decisions, rooted in the other party's dependence.
segments.tr: - **Kanalmacht** — Die Fähigkeit eines Mitglieds, die Entscheidungen eines anderen zu beeinflussen, verwurzelt in der Abhängigkeit der anderen Partei.

segments.src: - **Channel captain** — The member with enough power and capability to coordinate the channel's overall strategy.
segments.tr: - **Kanalführer** — Das Mitglied mit ausreichender Macht und Fähigkeit, die Gesamtstrategie des Kanals zu koordinieren.

segments.src: - **Multichannel conflict** — Friction that arises when a supplier sells through its own direct channel and through third-party retailers at the same time.
segments.tr: - **Multi-Kanal-Konflikt** — Reibung, die auftritt, wenn ein Lieferant gleichzeitig über seinen eigenen direkten Kanal und über Dritthändler verkauft.

segments.src: - **Superordinate goal** — A shared objective bigger than either party's individual interest (e.g., growing total category demand), used to defuse conflict.
segments.tr: - **Übergeordnetes Ziel** — Ein gemeinsames Ziel, das größer ist als das individuelle Interesse beider Parteien (z.B. Wachstum der Gesamtkategorienachfrage), um Konflikte zu entschärfen.

segments.src: - **Vertical marketing system (VMS)** — A channel deliberately unified by ownership, contract, or one member's power, designed to reduce conflict by design rather than by negotiation.
segments.tr: - **Vertikales Marketingsystem (VMS)** — Ein Kanal bewusst vereinheitlicht durch Eigentum, Vertrag oder Macht eines Mitglieds, um Konflikte durch Design zu reduzieren, anstatt durch Verhandlung.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) C** — the conflict is between a supplier's direct channel and its retail partners serving the same shopper, which is multichannel conflict; it's also vertical in structure, but "multichannel" is the precise term for the DTC-vs-wholesale case.
segments.tr: *Antworten: **1) C** — Der Konflikt ist zwischen dem direkten Kanal eines Lieferanten und seinen Handelspartnern, die denselben Käufer bedienen, was ein Multi-Kanal-Konflikt ist; es ist auch vertikal strukturiert, aber "Multi-Kanal" ist die präzise Bezeichnung für den DTC-vs.-Großhandel-Fall.

segments.src: **2) B** — withholding supply or allocation is a penalty, which is coercive power (a promise of better terms would be reward power).
segments.tr: **2) B** — Das Zurückhalten von Angebot oder Zuteilung ist eine Strafe, was Erzwingungsmacht ist (ein Versprechen besserer Bedingungen wäre Belohnungsmacht).

segments.src: **3) X** — moderate, openly managed conflict is functional: it surfaces real problems and pushes both sides toward better plans.
segments.tr: **3) X** — Gemäßigte, offen verwaltete Konflikte sind funktional: sie bringen echte Probleme ans Licht und drücken beide Seiten zu besseren Plänen.

segments.src: Only dysfunctional conflict, where the goal shifts from solving the issue to beating the partner, needs to be shut down.*
segments.tr: Nur dysfunktionale Konflikte, bei denen das Ziel von der Problemlösung zum Besiegen des Partners verschoben wird, müssen beendet werden.*

segments.tr: Một sắc thái đáng giữ lại: không phải tất cả xung đột đều tồi tệ.

segments.src: Moderate, well-aired disagreement is **functional conflict** — it surfaces problems and forces better plans.
segments.tr: Bất đồng ý vừa phải, được thảo luận kỹ lưỡng là **xung đột chức năng** — nó phơi bày các vấn đề và buộc các kế hoạch tốt hơn.

segments.src: Conflict becomes **dysfunctional** when it stops being about the issue and starts being about winning.
segments.tr: Xung đột trở nên **rối loạn chức năng** khi nó không còn là vấn đề mà trở thành vấn đề chiến thắng.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong Cuộc Sống Hàng Ngày

segments.src: It's Saturday in Columbus, Ohio, and you want a specific running shoe.
segments.tr: Đó là thứ bảy ở Columbus, Ohio, và bạn muốn một đôi giày chạy bộ cụ thể.

segments.src: The brand's own site lists it at **$140**, in an exclusive colorway you can't get anywhere else, and gives you loyalty points and free returns.
segments.tr: Trang web của chính thương hiệu liệt kê nó ở **$140**, trong một phối màu độc quyền mà bạn không thể nhận được ở bất cứ đâu khác, và cấp cho bạn các điểm trung thành và hoàn trả miễn phí.

segments.src: The Foot Locker two miles away has the same silhouette — but not that colorway — also at $140, because a **MAP (Minimum Advertised Price) policy** prevents the store from advertising it any lower.
segments.tr: Foot Locker cách đó hai dặm có hình dáng giống nhau — nhưng không phải phối màu đó — cũng ở $140, vì **chính sách MAP (Giá quảng cáo tối thiểu)** ngăn cửa hàng quảng cáo nó thấp hơn.

segments.src: So you order online.
segments.tr: Vì vậy, bạn đặt hàng trực tuyến.

segments.src: So does everyone else.
segments.tr: Tất cả mọi người cũng vậy.

segments.src: Now watch the conflict unfold.
segments.tr: Bây giờ hãy xem xung đột diễn ra.

segments.src: The retailer sees its best-selling brand siphoning off customers with better product and better perks, so it hands prime floor space to a rival brand and orders 30% less next season.
segments.tr: Nhà bán lẻ thấy thương hiệu bán chạy nhất của nó hút khách hàng với sản phẩm tốt hơn và lợi ích tốt hơn, vì vậy nó trao không gian sàn chính cho một thương hiệu đối thủ và đặt hàng ít hơn 30% mùa tới.

segments.src: The brand suddenly loses the discovery engine — the wall where people actually try shoes on — and its DTC growth stalls.
segments.tr: Thương hiệu đột nhiên mất công cụ khám phá — bức tường nơi mọi người thực sự thử giày — và tăng trưởng DTC của nó dừng lại.

segments.src: Both sides used their power.
segments.tr: Cả hai bên đều sử dụng quyền lực của họ.

segments.src: Both sides lost.
segments.tr: Cả hai bên đều thua.

segments.src: This isn't hypothetical.
segments.tr: Đây không phải là giả thuyết.

segments.src: Over the last decade several major athletic and apparel brands pulled sharply back from wholesale to go direct, then spent the following years rebuilding those same retail relationships after discovering that stores drive discovery, trial, and reach that a website can't replicate.
segments.tr: Trong thập kỷ qua, một số thương hiệu thể thao và thời trang lớn đã rút lại mạnh mẽ khỏi bán buôn để đi trực tiếp, sau đó dành những năm tiếp theo để xây dựng lại những quan hệ bán lẻ tương tự sau khi phát hiện ra rằng các cửa hàng thúc đẩy khám phá, thử nghiệm và phạm vi mà một trang web không thể sao chép.

segments.src: What a well-managed version looks like: **channel-specific assortments** (exclusive colorways for the store, too, not just the site), **shared inventory and sell-through data** so both sides forecast off the same numbers, **buy-online-pick-up-in-store** where the store gets credit for the sale, and a **joint business plan** signed once a year that states what each side owes the other.
segments.tr: Phiên bản được quản lý tốt trông như thế nào: **phân loại dành riêng cho kênh** (phối màu độc quyền cho cửa hàng, cũng không chỉ trang web), **dữ liệu hàng tồn kho và bán qua chung** để cả hai bên dự báo từ các số giống nhau, **mua trực tuyến-nhận hàng tại cửa hàng** nơi cửa hàng nhận tín dụng cho lần bán, và **kế hoạch kinh doanh chung** được ký một lần một năm nêu rõ từng bên nợ bên kia.

segments.src: Same two companies, same power, completely different outcome.
segments.tr: Cùng hai công ty, cùng quyền lực, kết quả hoàn toàn khác nhau.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt Ba dòng

segments.src: 1. Distribution channels are made of independent firms with conflicting goals, so conflict is structural, not a personality problem.
segments.tr: 1. Các kênh phân phối được tạo thành từ các công ty độc lập với các mục tiêu xung đột, vì vậy xung đột là cấu trúc, không phải vấn đề tính cách.

segments.src: 2. Power comes from reward, coercion, legitimacy, expertise, and reference — and it flows in both directions, so leaning on it alone invites retaliation.
segments.tr: 2. Quyền lực xuất phát từ phần thưởng, ép buộc, hợp pháp, chuyên môn và tham chiếu — và nó chảy theo cả hai hướng, vì vậy chỉ dựa vào nó sẽ mời trả đũa.

segments.src: 3. The durable fix is partnership: shared goals, clear roles, shared data, and aligned incentives that make cooperation more profitable than winning.
segments.tr: 3. Giải pháp bền vững là quan hệ đối tác: mục tiêu chung, vai trò rõ ràng, dữ liệu chung và các ưu đãi phù hợp khiến hợp tác có lợi nhuận hơn so với chiến thắng.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Tự kiểm tra

segments.src: **1.** A shoe brand's own website and the department store that carries it compete for the same shopper.
segments.tr: **1.** Trang web riêng của thương hiệu giày và cửa hàng bách hóa bán nó cạnh tranh cho cùng một khách hàng.

segments.src: What type of conflict is this?
segments.tr: Đây là loại xung đột nào?

segments.src: A) Horizontal conflict
segments.tr: A) Xung đột ngang

segments.src: B) Vertical conflict
segments.tr: B) Xung đột dọc

segments.src: C) Multichannel (cross-channel) conflict
segments.tr: C) Xung đột đa kênh (xuyên kênh)

segments.src: D) Functional conflict
segments.tr: D) Xung đột chức năng

segments.src: **2.** A supplier tells a retailer: "Miss your volume target and we'll cut your allocation next season."
segments.tr: **2.** Một nhà cung cấp nói với một nhà bán lẻ: "Không đạt được mục tiêu khối lượng của bạn và chúng tôi sẽ cắt giảm hạn mức của bạn mùa tới."

segments.src: Which source of power is being used?
segments.tr: Nguồn quyền lực nào đang được sử dụng?

segments.src: A) Referent power
segments.tr: A) Quyền lực tham chiếu

segments.src: B) Coercive power
segments.tr: B) Quyền lực cưỡng chế

segments.src: C) Expert power
segments.tr: C) Quyền lực chuyên gia

segments.src: D) Legitimate power
segments.tr: D) Quyền lực hợp pháp

segments.src: **3.** **O / X** — All channel conflict is harmful and should be eliminated.
segments.tr: **3.** **O / X** — Tất cả xung đột kênh đều có hại và nên được loại bỏ.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Các thuật ngữ Hôm nay

segments.src: - **Distribution channel** — The set of independent firms that move a product from producer to final customer.
segments.tr: - **Kênh phân phối** — Tập hợp các công ty độc lập di chuyển sản phẩm từ nhà sản xuất đến khách hàng cuối cùng.

segments.src: - **Channel power** — One member's ability to influence another's decisions, rooted in the other party's dependence.
segments.tr: - **Quyền lực kênh** — Khả năng của một thành viên để ảnh hưởng đến các quyết định của người khác, có gốc rễ trong sự phụ thuộc của bên kia.

segments.src: - **Channel captain** — The member with enough power and capability to coordinate the channel's overall strategy.
segments.tr: - **Thuyền trưởng kênh** — Thành viên có đủ quyền lực và khả năng để phối hợp chiến lược tổng thể của kênh.

segments.src: - **Multichannel conflict** — Friction that arises when a supplier sells through its own direct channel and through third-party retailers at the same time.
segments.tr: - **Xung đột đa kênh** — Sự ma sát phát sinh khi một nhà cung cấp bán qua kênh trực tiếp của riêng nó và thông qua các nhà bán lẻ bên thứ ba cùng một lúc.

segments.src: - **Superordinate goal** — A shared objective bigger than either party's individual interest (e.g., growing total category demand), used to defuse conflict.
segments.tr: - **Mục tiêu cấp cao hơn** — Một mục tiêu chung lớn hơn lợi ích cá nhân của bất kỳ bên nào (ví dụ, tăng tổng nhu cầu danh mục), được sử dụng để làm dịu xung đột.

segments.src: - **Vertical marketing system (VMS)** — A channel deliberately unified by ownership, contract, or one member's power, designed to reduce conflict by design rather than by negotiation.
segments.tr: - **Hệ thống tiếp thị dọc (VMS)** — Một kênh được thống nhất có chủ đích bằng quyền sở hữu, hợp đồng, hoặc quyền lực của một thành viên, được thiết kế để giảm xung đột bằng thiết kế hơn là bằng đàm phán.

segments.src: *Answers: **1) C** — the conflict is between a supplier's direct channel and its retail partners serving the same shopper, which is multichannel conflict; it's also vertical in structure, but "multichannel" is the precise term for the DTC-vs-wholesale case.
segments.tr: *Trả lời: **1) C** — xung đột là giữa kênh trực tiếp của nhà cung cấp và các đối tác bán lẻ của nó phục vụ cùng một khách hàng, đó là xung đột đa kênh; nó cũng có cấu trúc dọc, nhưng "đa kênh" là thuật ngữ chính xác cho trường hợp DTC-vs-bán buôn.

segments.src: **2) B** — withholding supply or allocation is a penalty, which is coercive power (a promise of better terms would be reward power).
segments.tr: **2) B** — tước quyền cung cấp hoặc phân bổ là một hình phạt, đó là quyền lực cưỡng chế (một lời hứa về các điều khoản tốt hơn sẽ là quyền lực phần thưởng).

segments.src: **3) X** — moderate, openly managed conflict is functional: it surfaces real problems and pushes both sides toward better plans.
segments.tr: **3) X** — xung đột vừa phải, được quản lý công khai là chức năng: nó phơi bày các vấn đề thực tế và thúc đẩy cả hai bên theo hướng các kế hoạch tốt hơn.

segments.src: Only dysfunctional conflict, where the goal shifts from solving the issue to beating the partner, needs to be shut down.*
segments.tr: Chỉ xung đột rối loạn chức năng, nơi mục tiêu thay đổi từ giải quyết vấn đề thành đánh bại đối tác, cần phải bị tắt.*
